articles.summary: Betfair te ofrece el pronóstico del partido que enfrenta a Celta y Bournemouth en Balaídos correspondiente a la jornada 5 de la Europa League
articles.body: El Celta afronta una nueva jornada europea con la necesidad de recuperar terreno después de un comienzo irregular. El conjunto gallego cayó frente al Union SG en su último compromiso y apenas ha conseguido sumar tres puntos en las cuatro jornadas disputadas. Su único triunfo llegó ante el Celtic, un resultado que no ha tenido continuidad y que obliga a los de Claudio Giráldez a reaccionar si quieren mantener opciones de avanzar en la competición. El encuentro en Balaídos supone una buena oportunidad para cambiar la dinámica, aunque el rival que visita Vigo atraviesa un momento mucho más favorable. Favorito para el partido entre Celta y Bournemouth El Bournemouth se ha convertido en uno de los equipos más fiables de esta fase liga. El conjunto inglés ha ganado todos sus partidos en la Europa League y llega después de protagonizar una remontada a domicilio frente al Sparta Praga en la jornada anterior. Su pleno de victorias le permite afrontar la visita a Balaídos con confianza y como favorito para llevarse los tres puntos. Las cuotas de las mejores casas de apuestas reflejan esa ventaja, aunque también anticipan un encuentro sin un desequilibrio excesivo. Betfair ofrece una cuota de 3.50 por la victoria del Celta, de 3.50 por el empate y de 2.00 por el triunfo del Bournemouth. Ambos equipos marcan Los registros ofensivos de ambos conjuntos permiten contemplar un partido con posibilidades de goles en las dos porterías. El Celta ha protagonizado encuentros con ambos equipos marcando en tres de sus cuatro compromisos europeos, mientras que esta circunstancia se ha producido en dos de los cuatro partidos del Bournemouth. El equipo gallego suele encontrar recursos para generar peligro en ataque, aunque también ha mostrado ciertas dificultades para mantener su portería a cero. El conjunto inglés, por su parte, llega con una dinámica ganadora y capacidad para aprovechar los espacios que pueda dejar su rival. El mercado del sí aparece como una opción interesante dentro de las apuestas deportivas. Betfair ofrece una cuota de 1.66 por el ambos marcan y de 2.15 por el no. Número total de goles (Over/Under) La tendencia de ambos equipos en el mercado de goles apunta a un encuentro con opciones de superar los 2.5 tantos. El Celta ha rebasado esa línea en tres de sus cuatro partidos de la Europa League, mientras que el Bournemouth lo ha hecho en todos sus compromisos. Estos registros reflejan que los encuentros de ambos equipos suelen ofrecer alternativas ofensivas y marcadores con varios goles. La necesidad del conjunto gallego de buscar un resultado positivo y la confianza con la que llega el equipo inglés pueden favorecer un partido abierto. Betfair ofrece una cuota de 1.85 tanto por el over 2.5 goles como por el under. Número total de córners (Over/Under) El mercado de saques de esquina presenta una línea interesante a partir de los promedios registrados por ambos equipos en la competición. El Celta alcanza una media de 7.5 córners por encuentro, mientras que el Bournemouth se sitúa en 6.5. La suma de ambos registros asciende a 14 saques de esquina, una cifra que invita a considerar la posibilidad de superar la línea de 10.5 propuesta por Betfair. La actividad ofensiva de los dos conjuntos y su tendencia a generar llegadas por las bandas pueden contribuir a elevar el número de lanzamientos desde la esquina. La cuota para superar los 10.5 córners es de 2.30, mientras que el under se paga a 1.50.

articles.title: When will Logan Paul return to WWE? Madison Square Garden finally sets date for his in-ring comeback
articles.summary: Logan Paul is set to wrestle again. Madison Square Garden announced on Wednesday, Nov.
articles.body: Logan Paul is set to wrestle again. Madison Square Garden announced on Wednesday, Nov. 25, that the WWE star will be on the card for the company's Holiday Live Tour stop on Dec. 26, his first scheduled match since a torn triceps in May.The former United States Champion has been out for more than seven months. No opponent has been named, and WWE has not said what the match will look like. Paul has kept showing up on Raw with The Vision in the meantime, though only as a ringside presence.When will Logan Paul return to WWE?Paul is booked for WWE's Dec. 26 live show at the Garden in New York City. MSG revealed it on its official X account, @TheGarden. The post opened with "JUST ANNOUNCED!" and said Paul "will be in action at @WWE Holiday Live Tour at The Garden on Dec 26!" A graphic and a ticket link came with it.The stop also doubles as a live event debut for Paul, who joined the roster in 2022. A television return before Dec. 26 is possible, though nothing has been announced.Producer Michael Hayes told Paul in September that clearance would not come before November at the earliest. The Garden date sits past that mark, so the booking has some room built in. Counted from the May 23 injury, Dec. 26 is exactly 31 weeks later.How the triceps tear and The Vision shaped the layoffThe tear happened at Saturday Night's Main Event. Paul and Austin Theory were defending the World Tag Team Championships against The Street Profits when Angelo Dawkins' dive left Paul landing awkwardly on the arm. Surgery followed, and the early projection was about six months.An orthopedic surgeon cautioned that pushing the recovery too fast could hurt Paul for years. Paul vented in a September vlog, saying, "I'm tired of being sidelined." At one point, Paul told Paul Heyman the rehab was "ahead of schedule."TV work never stopped. On the Nov. 9 Raw, Paul slipped Bron Breakker brass knuckles and distracted the referee during Breakker's match against Oba Femi.The tag titles are gone, though. Theory thought he would have to give up the gold for both champions, but Heyman revealed he could keep defending with Breakker. The pair dropped the belts to Je'Von Evans and Penta at Crown Jewel in November.Bronson Reed, recently back from his own injury, broke ribs at the same show, and reports said the damage kept him in Riyadh for about a week. articles.title: Carolina Matovac returns to Sweden for “wedding errands” as Buffalo Sabres captain Rasmus Dahlin prepares for marriage
articles.summary: Carolina Matovac is back in Sweden, focusing on wedding preparations with Buffalo Sabres captain Rasmus Dahlin. After a challenging medical journey, the couple is moving toward their special day.
articles.body: Buffalo Sabers captain Rasmus Dahlin’s fiancee Carolina Matovac is back in Sweden and busy with wedding preparations. She posted a recent Instagram update that read, “Back home & a few more stops for wedding errands,” giving fans a look at the preparations leading up to their marriage.The update comes as another good moment for the couple after a difficult time in their lives. Matovac's return to Sweden also brings attention to the personal milestones she and Dahlin are preparing to celebrate following her recovery from a life-threatening medical emergency.Carolina Matovac shares wedding preparations update as Rasmus Dahlin supportsCarolina Matovac has shared a glimpse of her wedding preparations after returning to Sweden, with her latest Instagram caption mentioning several errands ahead of her marriage to Rasmus Dahlin.The post offers a personal update without confirming an official wedding date. Although the couple has not publicly announced when the ceremony will take place, Matovac's reference to wedding errands indicates that preparations are receiving attention.Carolina Matovac shares heartfelt message about her familyAlongside her wedding-related update, Matovac also shared an emotional message about her family on Instagram Stories."Of all the things my parents have given me, my sisters are the greatest gift," she wrote.Her message highlighted the importance of family support as she enters another significant chapter of her life. Returning to Sweden also brings her closer to the people who supported her during an exceptionally difficult period.Rasmus Dahlin reflects on his fiancée's recoveryRasmus Dahlin has previously spoken about the difficult experience of watching his fiancée face a serious medical emergency.The couple was on vacation in France in the summer of 2025 when Matovac fell critically ill. Her condition worsened to severe heart failure and required emergency medical intervention, including CPR and eventually a heart transplant.Her recovery continued in Gothenburg, Sweden, while Dahlin balanced his responsibilities with the Buffalo Sabres and made trips to be with her.Buffalo Sabres captain recalls emotional reception in BuffaloOne particularly memorable moment came when Matovac returned to Buffalo and attended a Sabres game against the Boston Bruins on March 25.She received a standing ovation from the crowd at KeyBank Center when the arena welcomed her back. The reception moved Dahlin, who later expressed gratitude for the support shown to his fiancée."Unbelievable. The support we've had for a long time now, and her getting this today was special. She had to go through a lot of testing, so I'm happy she's here," Dahlin said.Reflecting further on the moment, he added:"That was so special. Also very, very special for her. They gave her a standing ovation. It was unbelievable. I did not expect that. It wasn't easy playing that game, that's for sure. I'm just so happy for her."The emotional reception reflected the support surrounding the couple throughout Matovac's recovery.Her latest Sweden update now shifts attention toward wedding preparations and the future. articles.title: Michael van Gerwen 'buzzing' for World Darts Championship and ready to take early trip to new-look Alexandra Palace
articles.summary: Michael van Gerwen reached the Grand Slam of Darts semi-finals and is among the favourites for the World Darts Championship, beginning December 11 live on Sky Sports; Van Gerwen previously won the Sid Waddell Trophy in 2014, 2017 and 2019
articles.body:
The Dutchman produced an impressive run to the Grand Slam of Darts semi-finals earlier this month, where he fired a nine-darter in the first leg of his quarter-final victory over Tom Sykes before being knocked out by compatriot Gian van Veen.

Van Gerwen is keen to build on his Wolverhampton performance at this weekend's Players Championship Finals ahead of turning attention to the Worlds, where he will be among the favourites to lift the Sid Waddell Trophy.

"That [consistency] is what you also need, especially at this time of year - you want to do yourself favours," Van Gerwen told Sky Sports . "We all know I had a tough period but you need to move on.

"You can't sit still and do nothing - you have to practise, you have to put time and effort in to produce some good darts. The field is wide, there's so many good players now, so you have to move along.

"I'm feeling okay, my game is starting to get in a good place. The consistency was there in the semi-final [of the Grand Slam], I missed too many doubles. You can't look back anymore because the World Championship is on the horizon."

Record crowds will be expected throughout this year's edition, which moves into Alexandra Palace's Great Hall and offers over 5,000 fans a session, with Van Gerwen keen to look at the new layout ahead of his world title challenge.

"When I go to London, as soon as I know when I play, two days before, I'm going to have a look [at Alexandra Palace] and see what's going on," Van Gerwen added.

"I'm one of the more prepared ones because you can't let yourself down in any way by thinking, 'I should have done this, I should have done that' - just do it!

"It [winning] would mean the world to me, but first let me win the first round, the second round and then go off, because it's going to be a long few weeks."

Can 'consistent' Van Veen challenge for world title?

Van Veen finished runner-up to Gerwyn Price in Wolverhampton, extending his strong season in TV tournaments, with the world No 2 keen to go one better than last year's runner-up finish to Luke Littler at Alexandra Palace.

"I showed [form] at the Grand Slam, a very good tournament there," Van Veen told Sky Sports . "Very disappointed to not get it over the line in the final but hopefully I can have a good run [at the Players Championship Finals] and then carry that form into the Worlds.

"Last year [at the Worlds], it was only [about] winning that one game. Now I've got all the experience of getting through to the final. Hopefully we can do that again this year."

On his rise to world No 2, Van Veen added: "A lot of players say it's because it's based on the ranking money and it's highly influenced by the World Championship, and it is, but everyone had the chance to do it at the Worlds and I took mine.

"This year has been very good, especially on the TV tournaments. Very consistent with semi-finals and now even a final, so I belong somewhere around No 2 in the world. Maybe top four, top six, but I'm very pleased to be the No 2 in the world right now."

articles.title: UK Championship: Mark Selby faces tough opener, with Mark Allen and Ronnie O'Sullivan set to feature
articles.summary: Mark Selby is to start his defence of the UK Championship title against Matt Selt on Saturday in York.
articles.body:
Four-time world champion Mark Selby will begin his defence of the UK Championship title against Matt Selt on Saturday at York Barbican.

It represents a tough opening match for Selby, with fellow Englishman Selt having beaten world number 17 Jak Jones, the highest-ranked player in the qualifiers, to reach the televised stages.

Mark Allen, who spoke of his mental health struggles in an emotional interview last month, is set to face Yuan Sijun.

Allen, from Antrim, lost to his friend Jordan Brown in the first round of the Northern Ireland Open in October after five months away from the sport.

Prior to that, Allen had not played since missing what would have been a match-winning black off its spot in the World Championship semi-final against eventual champion Wu Yize in May.

Record eight-time UK Championship winner Ronnie O'Sullivan, whose form has deserted him since reaching the semi-finals of the Wuhan Open in August, will play Jack Lisowski in the first round.

"What an explosive encounter that will be. It is going to be quickfire stuff with 15, 16 or 17 seconds a shot from both players," said former world champion Ken Doherty.

"You don't know what to expect from Ronnie O'Sullivan but he is a mercurial genius and an enigma. He could turn up and just flick a switch and be flying."

World number one Zhao Xintong will meet debutant Dylan Emery, while world champion Wu Yize gets under way against qualifier Michael Holt.

Elsewhere, John Higgins, 51, is up against one of snooker's new generation in 20-year-old Artemijs Zizins, who is the first Latvian player to reach the final stages of a Triple Crown event.

Mark Williams will play Stephen Maguire - the winner in 2004 and also twice a finalist in 2007 and 2019 - and Judd Trump will come up against Hossein Vafaei or Ben Mertens.

Kyren Wilson, who is in a rich vein of form after winning the Champion of Champions, the International Championship and the Northern Ireland Open already this autumn, begins his quest to reach a first UK final against Fan Zhengyi.

The first Triple Crown event of the season, which will be shown live on the BBC, takes place from 28 November to 6 December and offers a top prize of £312,500.

UK Championship match schedule, seeds & BBC TV coverage

Lisowski & Ding among familiar faces to qualify

Former semi-finalist Lisowski set up a mouthwatering contest with O'Sullivan with a 6-4 victory over Mark Joyce late on Thursday evening.

"I stayed away from it all day. I thought 'my treat if I win will be to look and see who I have got' and it's Ronnie isn't it?" Lisowski said.

"It's as big as it gets. It's a very tough game obviously. He's the greatest player ever and I am not ecstatic about it [the draw]."

When Ding Junhui trailed 5-3 to Robbie Williams earlier in the day he looked set to miss the televised stages of the tournament for the first time since his debut in 2004.

However, the three-time champion rallied and made a break of 79 in the decider to secure his spot against Ali Carter on Monday afternoon.

From 2-1 behind, Maguire hit form to reel off five frames in a row with breaks of 52, 118, 65, 101 and 73, with two-time winner Williams now lying in wait in the opening session on Saturday at 13:00 GMT.

Zhou Yuelong became the ninth player from China to reach the first round with a 6-4 victory over Daniel Wells and he could earn a spot at the Masters in January if he enjoys a lengthy run in the tournament.

Yuan took four consecutive frames on his way to a 6-4 win over 2023 Crucible champion Luca Brecel.

Meanwhile, Hossein Vafaei led 5-0 before sealing a 6-3 success against Ben Mertens, Thailand's Thepchaiya Un-Nooh came through a seesaw encounter to defeat Zak Surety 6-5 and Welshman Emery defeated Scott Donaldson 6-3.

articles.title: El "Ferrari volador" incorpora a un nuevo regatista para un desafío épico
articles.standfirst: Ferrari Hypersail ficha al británico Simon Fisher, que se une a Voltolini, Conti y Falcone. Lo anuncia en el Yacht Club Italiano, que se convierte en colaborador de 'Il Cavallino Rampante'
articles.summary: Ferrari Hypersail ficha al británico Simon Fisher, que se une a Voltolini, Conti y Falcone. Lo anuncia en el Yacht Club Italiano, que se convierte en colaborador de 'Il Cavallino Rampante'
articles.body: La tradición náutica italiana tiene uno de sus grandes referentes en el Yacht Club Italiano. Fundado en Génova en 1879, es el club de vela más antiguo del país y uno de los veteranos del Mediterráneo. Representa una cultura de navegación y competición que forma parte del ADN deportivo italiano. Entre sus miembros históricos figura, entre otros, Guglielmo Marconi, creador de la radiotransmisión a larga distancia y que realizó experimentos a bordo de su barco Elettra. También está la Casa de Saboya. Dos de sus ilustres tienen estatua en las escalera principal. En su sede histórica en el Porticciolo Duca degli Abruzzi se ha presentado este jueves la colaboración con Ferrari Hypersail, el monocasco volador de 100 pies (30 metros) de Il Cavallino Rampante. O lo que es lo mismo, el 'bólido' del mar diseñado para devorar récords en el océano a 100 km/hora. Su objetivo final es intentar batir el récord de la vuelta al mundo a vela, el Trofeo Julio Verne, en menos de 40 días. El récord actual lo tiene el Sodebo francés que empleó 40 días, 10 horas, 45 minutos y 50 segundos. La sinergia entre el legado de Ferrari en ingeniería y su cultura del rendimiento y la consolidada tradición náutica del Yacht Club Italiano, del que lucirá su gallardete, se dieron la mano en una exclusiva presentación a que asistió hasta el ministro italiano de Deportes Andrea Abodi y que contó con MARCA como testigo. El barco, que ya tiene el casco terminado, comenzó a diseñarse en Maranello con los ingenieros de Ferrari, se ha construido en un astillero cerca de Pisa y tendrá su base de entrenamiento en Livorno. Hasta allí se trasladará en pocos días y entrará en una nueva fase. "Con Ferrari Hypersail estamos dando forma a una nueva visión: crear un “Ferrari que vuela” capaz de afrontar uno de los retos más ambiciosos, el océano. Es un proyecto que expresa plenamente nuestra manera de entender la innovación y ese ingenio italiano que Ferrari representa. Este reto pretende hacer volar a Ferrari, algo que, en sí mismo, nos lleva no solo de la pista al mar, sino del mar al aire", reconocía John Elkann, presidente de Ferrari y socio del Yacht Club desde 2005. "Nuestra ambición es dar la vuelta al mundo batiendo récords y, sobre todo, aportar no solo una dimensión de rendimiento —es decir, ser rápidos—, sino también la de ser resistentes, y esta doble dimensión es aún más difícil de alcanzar. Hemos puesto nuestra pasión y competencia al servicio de lo imposible", añadió a la vez que confesó que la idea surgió durante el Covid junto al navegante Giovanni Soldini. La pregunta fue: ¿Cómo de rápido y cómo de lejos podemos llegar?". No sólo se trata de dar la vuelta al mundo en el menor tiempo posible sino de hacerlo full foiling, es decir, volando el cien por cien del tiempo sobre el mar gracias dos foils laterales y una quilla basculante en un monocasco, algo nunca visto hasta ahora. Frente a las configuraciones convencionales, Ferrari Hypersail introduce un tercer punto de apoyo para gestionar el vuelo y mantener el equilibrio del barco. El reto es mayúsculo. La tripulación estará formada por entre 8 y 12 navegantes. Hasta hoy se conocían los nombres de Enrico Voltolini, navegante y líder del proyecto Ferrari Hypersail; Giulia Conti, olímpica en tres clases diferentes, campeona mundial y europea de 49er FX y ganadora de la primera Copa América femenina con el Luna Rossa; y Shannon Falcone, que ha participado en seis Copas América -ha ganado dos-, y ha dado dos vueltas al mundo (The Ocean Race). Este jueves se ha desvelado la última incorporación al equipo, el británico Simon Fisher. 'SiFi' es uno de los navegantes oceánicos más experimentados de su generación. Combina navegación estratégica, conocimiento técnico, experiencia en Copa América y miles de millas en regatas alrededor del mundo. Es dos veces ganador de The Ocean Race (2014-2015 y 2022-2023) y galardonado con el prestigioso premio individual “Magnus Olsson”. "Es un tremendo honor y privilegio formar parte de Ferrari Hypersail. Cuando Enrique se puso en contacto conmigo para participar en este proyecto, no lo dudé ni un instante. Creo que lo verdaderamente único de este proyecto es cómo aúna lo mejor del mundo de la vela y lo mejor de la industria automovilística, además de la tecnología", dijo Fisher, que ejercerá como navegante y formará parte del equipo de Rendimiento y Adquisición de Datos (Performance & Data Acquisition), contribuyendo al desarrollo de metodologías de recopilación, análisis e interpretación de datos a bordo. "Se sitúa en la vanguardia de la navegación de alta mar y supone una oportunidad para redefinir lo que entendemos por navegación de alta mar. Por eso, estoy muy ilusionado por embarcarme en esta aventura", añadió.

articles.title: Phil Taylor and Adrian Lewis suffer five straight defeats at Modus Super Series International Pairs
articles.summary: Phil Taylor came out of retirement to partner Adrian Lewis for England at Thursday's Modus Super Series International Pairs Tournament in Portsmouth, but the duo endured a disappointing return, losing all five of their matches; Taylor retired from professional darts in 2018
articles.body:
Taylor, now 66, retired from the competitive circuit in 2018, five years after claiming his 16th and final world title. However, the 16-time world champion returned to action to partner his long-time friend Lewis for the tournament.

Their opening match on Thursday saw them face Scotland's John Henderson and Robert Thornton, with the England pair suffering a narrow 4-3 defeat.

Things failed to improve in their second outing, as Taylor and Lewis were beaten 4-2 by Sweden's Andreas Harrysson and Anton Ostlund.

A shock 4-3 defeat to unheralded Swiss duo Ansh Sood and Marcel Walpen followed, before Taylor and Lewis suffered a fourth consecutive loss, going down 4-1 to Germany's Daniel Klose and Liam Maendl-Lawrance.

Their fifth and final group-stage outing saw England take a 2-1 lead against Denmark, the only other side in their pool yet to record a victory. However, Ivan Springborg Poulsen and Andreas Toft Jorgensen responded by winning the next three legs in succession to condemn the English pair to a 4-2 defeat and a fifth straight loss.

Taylor revealed in September that the opportunity to partner Lewis was enough to tempt him back to the oche, although his return is not expected to signal a permanent comeback.

The 16-time world champion, who recently underwent successful hip replacement surgery, previously enjoyed considerable success alongside Lewis, with the pair winning four World Cup of Darts titles together.

The Modus Super Series International Pairs Tournament continues in Portsmouth until November 28.

articles.body: Trinity Rodman and Ben Shelton have seemingly taken different approaches to life after reports of their breakup, with both sharing Instagram posts just a day after news of their split surfaced. Rodman posted a short message about resetting and trusting the process, while Shelton shared a photo collection featuring tennis, cars and other moments alongside a “Life Is Good” remix, leaving fans reading between the lines.Trinity Rodman’s Instagram message comes after reports of her breakup with Ben SheltonRodman shared her Instagram story while travelling on a flight, posting a selfie with the words, “Trust the process. Reset time.” The brief message came shortly after reports claimed that the couple had ended their relationship, which had lasted nearly two years.Although Rodman did not directly mention Shelton or confirm the reported split, her post quickly attracted attention because of the timing. The Washington Spirit forward has had a demanding period, with the team recently falling short in the NWSL Final against the Kansas City Current.The Spirit lost the match 2-1, marking another difficult ending to their season. Rodman also suffered a shoulder injury during the game, which will keep her out of the upcoming CONCACAF W Championship with the U.S. women’s national team. The tennis player uploaded several pictures showing different parts of his life, including moments on the court, wearing a suit and posing around cars and what appeared to be a new home. He used a 🔁 emoji as the caption and added the “Life Is Good” remix as the background music.The timing and tone of the post led some followers to connect it with the breakup reports. One commenter described it as “This is that newly single photo dump energy,” while another joked, “Ben Shelton : Hi, I’m ok !” However, neither athlete directly addressed the reports or confirmed that their relationship had ended.Ben Shelton and Trinity Rodman’s long distance relationship had become difficultThe reported breakup comes after both athletes spoke about the challenges of managing their relationship while competing in different sports and travelling frequently.Shelton had previously discussed the difficulties in an interview with US Weekly, admitting that finding time for each other was not always easy, even when they had days off.“I think what a lot of people don’t see is when we actually do have time or a couple of days off, we’re so exhausted that it’s tough to do anything,” Shelton said. “It is tough to make time.”Their schedules also meant that they were in different cities during important moments. Shelton was not present at Rodman’s NWSL Final against the Kansas City Current on Saturday, as he was competing at the ATP Finals in Turin, Italy. He lost his semifinal match to Carlos Alcaraz that same day.The couple first made their relationship public in March 2025 and were often seen supporting each other despite their busy schedules. Rodman even travelled between Washington, D.C., and New York during the NWSL season to watch Shelton compete at the US Open.While the latest Instagram posts have sparked speculation about what happened between them, neither Rodman nor Shelton has publicly confirmed the breakup or explained whether they are moving on from their relationship.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. articles.title: Luke Humphries ‘feeling much better’ after trapped nerve threatened Players Championship Finals hopes
articles.summary: Luke Humphries is confident he can get back to performing at his best at this week's Players Championship Finals after injuries have blighted his form; Humphries suffered a shock exit at the Grand Slam of Darts and is hoping for 'injury free' end to the year
articles.body:
Humphries was seen wincing in pain during his shock Grand Slam exit to Tom Sykes and later cast doubt on social media about whether he would feature in this week's tournament.

On Thursday, the 31-year-old revealed that he had been managing the injury for some time.

"Unfortunately, [my season] has taken a little stride back last week with the trapped nerve in my back; it's a recurring thing that's happened quite a few times now," Humphries told Sky Sports .

"I'm going to have to get it sorted and find ways to stop it from coming back, because when you're playing in major tournaments, the last thing you need is that kind of thing lingering.

"It's much better now; after a week off, it's much more repaired. Hopefully, going into the Players Championship Finals this weekend, I can play injury-free, and hopefully I go on to win."

Humphries expressed his frustration at how injuries and illness have hampered the back end of his season.

The Englishman had hoped to build on his World Grand Prix victory and win his first European Championship, but was forced to withdraw from October's tournament due to illness .

"It's quite unfortunate because I've been playing really good," Humphries said.

"The European Championships I had to [withdraw] because I wasn't well. So, it's been a little bit of a disappointment for me in the past couple of majors, after I won the Grand Prix.

"I was looking to cash in on that and do really well."

Humphries is out to win his third Players Championship Finals this week and will play Darryl Pilgrim in the opening round on Friday night in Minehead.

Humphries added he has been working hard alongside his physio to reduce the effects of the injury and if he can do that, he backs himself to get back to playing his best.

"It's just something you can't stop. There's nothing you can do about it. It's not like I'm doing anything to make it happen," he said.

"It's just something that recurs, and something that me and my physio, John, we're working through and are trying to build a bit of strength in it and stop it recurring.

"If I can stay injury-free, everyone knows how well I play and the consistency I [have] showed this year.

"Hopefully an injury-free back of the year."

The 2026 National Dog Show was a crowning moment for Rocker, as the Black and Tan Coonhound was crowned Best in Show.

Rocker was bestowed the honor from a collection of 2,107 dogs that started the competition, including three first-time breeds in the Teddy Roosevelt Terrier, Basset Fauve De Bretagne and Russian Tsvetnaya Bolonka.

"When he goes around, he's an athlete," judge Lorraine Bisso said about Rocker (h/t Nate Ryan of NBC Sports). "You can see him out there hunting in the woods. He's just a beautiful dog. When you judge coonhounds, you try to picture them trailing. He has beautiful feet and a lovely forechest, which is necessary because he's going to run for 25 miles. articles.title: El 'Messi croata' de la Masía se ofrece a Millonarios, Junior y Santa Fe
articles.standfirst: Alen Halilovic, de jugar en Barcelona y Milan a sonar en Millonarios, Santa Fe y Junior
articles.summary: Alen Halilovic, de jugar en Barcelona y Milan a sonar en Millonarios, Santa Fe y Junior
articles.body: El mercado de pases del fútbol colombiano volvió a sorprender con un nombre de alto perfil: Alen Halilović, mediocampista croata de 30 años, formado en La Masía del FC Barcelona y con paso por el AC Milan. Según reportes del periodista Alexis Rodríguez, el jugador habría sido ofrecido a Junior de Barranquilla, Millonarios e Independiente Santa Fe, aunque por ahora no existe una negociación avanzada ni un acuerdo confirmado con alguno de los tres clubes. La noticia llama la atención porque Halilović no es un futbolista cualquiera en términos de currículo. Fue considerado una de las mayores promesas europeas de su generación, recibió el apodo de “Messi croata” durante su etapa formativa en Barcelona y compartió vestuarios con figuras de élite. Sin embargo, su trayectoria también es un caso de estudio sobre la presión, las lesiones y la dificultad de convertir talento juvenil en una carrera de primer nivel sostenida. Halilović nació en Dubrovnik, Croacia, y se formó futbolísticamente en el Dinamo Zagreb, uno de los clubes más importantes del fútbol balcánico y una histórica fábrica de talentos. Su habilidad para conducir, asociarse en espacios cortos, atacar desde el mediocampo y definir lo llevaron muy joven a ser comparado con Lionel Messi, una etiqueta que después se convirtió en una carga tan grande como un reconocimiento. El Barcelona lo incorporó en 2014, cuando apenas tenía 18 años. La expectativa era enorme: el club catalán veía en él un mediapunta de futuro, con condiciones técnicas para adaptarse a su estilo de juego. Pero su paso por el primer equipo fue mínimo: disputó un solo partido oficial con el Barcelona y apenas 28 minutos, según las estadísticas. Eso no significa que su etapa barcelonista careciera de valor. Halilović jugó 29 partidos con el segundo equipo del Barça, acumuló 1.756 minutos y tuvo la oportunidad de formarse en un entorno de altísimo nivel. Aun así, la competencia interna, las expectativas desmedidas y la necesidad de sumar minutos lo llevaron a buscar continuidad fuera del club. El apodo de “Messi croata” nació precisamente en sus años de formación. No era una comparación casual: Halilović tenía perfil zurdo, buena conducción, visión, regate y capacidad para aparecer entre líneas, rasgos que evocaban al argentino en su juventud. Pero las comparaciones con Messi suelen ser una trampa. Pocas veces un jugador joven puede soportar semejante estándar, y en el caso de Halilović la expectativa pública terminó siendo más ruidosa que su desarrollo deportivo. Su carrera no fue un fracaso absoluto —llegó a jugar en Barcelona, Milan, Hamburgo, Standard de Lieja, Sporting de Gijón, Heerenveen y Fortuna Sittard—, pero sí quedó lejos del nivel de estrella mundial que muchos anticipaban. La trayectoria de Halilović puede dividirse en tres etapas: la promesa del Dinamo Zagreb, la búsqueda de continuidad en Europa y la recuperación competitiva en Países Bajos. En el AC Milan, por ejemplo, solo disputó tres partidos y 59 minutos, lo que refleja lo difícil que fue para él ganarse un lugar en un plantel de alto nivel. Su paso por el fútbol inglés, alemán, belga, español y neerlandés demuestra, sin embargo, que siempre tuvo mercado y que varios clubes vieron en su talento una apuesta interesante. La etapa más sólida de Halilović llegó en el Fortuna Sittard de la Eredivisie. Allí encontró continuidad, protagonismo y una función clara como mediocampista ofensivo. Entre 2023 y 2026 jugó 67 partidos, anotó siete goles y repartió siete asistencias; además, acumuló 4.223 minutos, la mayor cantidad de su carrera profesional. Ese periodo es importante para entender por qué su nombre aparece ahora en Colombia. No se trata de un jugador retirado ni de una figura que llega únicamente por marketing: Halilović demostró en Países Bajos que todavía puede competir, crear juego y aportar en el último tercio. Su contrato con Fortuna Sittard terminó en junio de 2026 y, desde entonces, permanece como agente libre. Esa situación abre la puerta a una incorporación sin costo de traspaso, aunque el salario, la comisión de los representantes y la condición física del jugador seguirán siendo variables decisivas. El principal obstáculo de Halilović ha sido la continuidad. Entre abril y noviembre de 2025 estuvo 237 días fuera de las canchas por una lesión de tobillo, una ausencia que interrumpió su mejor momento en Fortuna Sittard. Aunque ya está recuperado, lleva varios meses sin disputar partidos oficiales. Para cualquier club colombiano, eso implica un riesgo deportivo evidente: necesitará un proceso de puesta a punto, control médico riguroso y paciencia antes de poder rendir al nivel que exige la Liga BetPlay. No es un problema menor. En el fútbol colombiano, los fichajes de jugadores con historial de lesiones suelen requerir una planificación cuidadosa, especialmente si el club espera que sean piezas determinantes desde el inicio del torneo. La experiencia de Halilović sugiere que, de concretarse su llegada, debería evaluarse primero su estado físico y luego su rol dentro del sistema táctico. La información sobre su ofrecimiento a Junior, Millonarios y Santa Fe fue difundida por Alexis Rodríguez, periodista especializado en mercado de pases, a través de su cuenta de X. Varios medios colombianos retomaron la versión, pero todos coinciden en que se trata de una posibilidad explorada por sus representantes, no de un fichaje cerrado. El atractivo es claro: Halilović tiene nombre internacional, experiencia en clubes grandes y un perfil que puede encajar en un equipo que necesite más creación. Para Junior, Millonarios o Santa Fe, incorporarlo sería un golpe de mercado y de comunicación, especialmente en un momento en que la Liga BetPlay ha vuelto a recibir jugadores con pasado relevante en Europa. Además, el futbolista croata podría encontrar en Colombia un contexto competitivo menos expuesto que las grandes ligas europeas, con posibilidad de ser protagonista. La Liga BetPlay ya cuenta con nombres de larga trayectoria internacional como James Rodríguez, Juan Guillermo Cuadrado, Hugo Rodallega, Jackson Martínez y Carlos Bacca, lo que refuerza la idea de que el torneo se ha convertido en una alternativa atractiva para figuras experimentadas.

articles.title: Gukesh's berlin defence masterclass holds Sindarov to draw in game 3 of World Championship
articles.summary: Reigning world champion D Gukesh produced a composed display with the black pieces to hold Uzbek challenger Javokhir Sindarov to a draw in Game 3 of the
articles.body: Reigning world champion D Gukesh produced a composed display with the black pieces to hold Uzbek challenger Javokhir Sindarov to a draw in Game 3 of the World Chess Championship in Geneva on Thursday. Deploying the formidable Berlin Defence, the Indian ace neutralised Sindarov's attacking attempts and ensured the contest remained level.The third game ended in a draw after 60 moves, leaving both players tied at 1.5 points apiece heading into Friday's rest day. Gukesh will have the advantage of playing with the white pieces when the match resumes in Game 4.Gukesh's Berlin defence leaves Sindarov searching for answersGukesh appeared thoroughly prepared for the opening and handled Sindarov's attempts to gain an advantage with confidence. Despite computer evaluations occasionally favouring White, the Indian found the necessary moves to keep his position under control.The Berlin Defence has a rich history in world championship chess. The phrase "Berlin is in Geneva" echoes the famous use of the same opening by Vladimir Kramnik against Garry Kasparov during their 2000 World Championship match.Sindarov appeared caught off guard by Gukesh's preparation and spent considerable time navigating the opening. The Uzbek challenger eventually found himself under significant clock pressure, an unusual situation for Gukesh, who has often faced time trouble in his games with the black pieces.Sindarov tries to turn up the heat, but Gukesh holds firmAs the game progressed, Sindarov continued searching for ways to create an advantage. An aggressive kingside pawn advance briefly added tension to the position, but Gukesh remained unfazed and continued to find accurate defensive moves.The contest eventually moved into a rook-and-opposite-coloured-bishops endgame, where Sindarov attempted to increase the pressure. However, Gukesh's defensive accuracy left the challenger with little room to make progress.The Indian also enjoyed a significant advantage on the clock for much of the game. Sindarov faced a particularly difficult situation towards the end, needing to make four moves in the final two minutes before the additional 30 minutes were added to his clock. The Uzbek managed to reach the time control, with both players receiving the additional time and a 30-second increment per move. Neither could find a winning breakthrough, and the players eventually agreed to a draw after 60 moves.With three games completed, the World Championship match remains evenly poised at 1.5-1.5. Friday will be a rest day before the two players return to the board for Game 4.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Los secuestradores del Éxito de Cartagena se quedan dormidos tras comerse todo el pollo frito y beber whiskey
articles.standfirst: Capturados por el secuestro en el Éxito de Cartagena se quedaron dormidos en plena audiencia y la jueza los regañó
articles.summary: Capturados por el secuestro en el Éxito de Cartagena se quedaron dormidos en plena audiencia y la jueza los regañó
articles.body: La noticia que ha llamado la atención en Colombia no es solo el secuestro masivo ocurrido en el Éxito de La Castellana, en Cartagena, sino la escena registrada durante la audiencia judicial: dos hombres señalados de participar en la retención de 87 personas se quedaron dormidos y desviaron la mirada mientras la Fiscalía les imputaba cargos por secuestro extorsivo agravado. La jueza tuvo que interrumpir la diligencia, llamarles la atención y pedir que les suministraran agua para mantenerlos despiertos. La diligencia de legalización de captura e imputación de cargos se realizó en la madrugada del jueves 26 de noviembre de 2026, con los imputados Juan Camilo Torres Manco y Jhon Albeiro Mejía Blandón conectados desde el CDT Bellavista. Mientras la Fiscalía exponía los hechos relacionados con una retención que, según la acusación, duró más de 17 horas, ambos comenzaron a cabecear y parecían quedarse dormidos. La jueza del Juzgado 21 Penal Municipal con funciones de control de garantías interrumpió la audiencia y dijo: “Allá, por favor, el señor John Albeiro Mejía se está quedando dormido. Les agradezco estar atentos. Custodio, si tienen agua, que le suministren por lo menos”. Luego insistió en que los procesados debían mirar la cámara y escuchar con atención, porque la Fiscalía les estaba explicando los hechos, el delito imputado y las consecuencias procesales. La escena generó indignación y burla en redes sociales porque contrasta de forma extrema con la gravedad de los hechos que se les atribuyen: la Fiscalía sostiene que participaron en la toma de rehenes de 87 personas y que exigían más de 7.000 millones de pesos, dos camionetas blindadas y la liberación de una vía del sistema TransCaribe. Los dos hombres señalados son Juan Camilo Torres Manco y Jhon Albeiro Mejía Blandón. Ambos fueron capturados el 25 de noviembre, tras la intervención policial en el supermercado Éxito de La Castellana, en Cartagena. La Fiscalía les imputó el delito de secuestro extorsivo agravado, en calidad de coautores, por la retención de 87 personas. Según la entidad acusadora, los detenidos habrían utilizado a las víctimas como escudos humanos y habrían intentado camuflarse entre los rehenes para evitar su captura. En la audiencia, ambos rechazaron los cargos. Uno de ellos aseguró que él era un rehén y no un secuestrador, y la jueza le explicó que, si mantenía esa posición, el caso debería ir a juicio; si cambiaba de posición, podría allanarse a los cargos. Finalmente, Torres Manco y Mejía Blandón dijeron que no aceptaban la imputación. El caso de los “dormidos del Éxito” no es solo un hecho curioso o una anécdota viral. Es la continuación pública de un caso grave: un secuestro masivo en Cartagena, con decenas de víctimas, un operativo policial, un presunto secuestrador abatido y dos capturados que ahora enfrentan cargos por secuestro extorsivo agravado. Lo que hizo que la audiencia se volviera noticia no fue solamente la imputación, sino el contraste entre la seriedad del proceso y la actitud de los imputados. Mientras la Fiscalía describía una retención de más de 17 horas, los dos señalados parecían incapaces de mantenerse despiertos, lo que obligó a la jueza a detener la diligencia y exigir atención. El elemento que más llamó la atención del caso no fue solo la duración del secuestro, sino el comportamiento de los captores una vez que su plan inicial falló. Lejos de mantener una actitud estrictamente táctica, varios de ellos habrían convertido parte de la noche en una especie de fiesta dentro del almacén. El alcalde de Cartagena, Dumek Turbay Paz, aseguró que los delincuentes consumieron alimentos y bebidas de alto valor del inventario del hipermercado. Según sus declaraciones, se comieron los pollos Frisby disponibles, tomaron licores costosos y algunos se cambiaron de ropa con prendas sustraídas de la tienda. “Terminó siendo un poquito chistoso el hecho de que se comieran todos los pollos Frisby, que se tomaran todos los licores de más alto valor, que se cambiaran de ropa algunos”, afirmó el mandatario, según recogió Blu Radio. Entre los licores mencionados por el alcalde están Macallan y Johnnie Walker Blue Label, conocidos popularmente como “Sello Azul”. Turbay precisó que los asaltantes consumieron “mucho” de estas bebidas durante el cautiverio. El episodio adquirió un tono aún más surrealista cuando, de acuerdo con la versión oficial, los captores obligaron a un entrenador de un gimnasio ubicado en el complejo comercial a actuar como mesero y servirles las copas. Testimonios de rehenes recogidos por otros medios coinciden en que los hombres armados bebieron alcohol frente a las víctimas. Héctor Puello, panadero del almacén, relató que los captores “estaban bastante tomados” y consumían whisky fino, incluyendo Sello Rojo y Old Parr. La música también hizo parte de la escena. Según el alcalde Turbay, los delincuentes reprodujeron corridos mexicanos a través de los parlantes del almacén, lo que reforzó la percepción de que el grupo había perdido el control de la situación. “Cuando estaban los corridos mexicanos sonando en los parlantes nuevos del centro comercial El Éxito, ya dijimos: ‘estos tipos no son cualquiera, o sea, están carnavaleados’”, declaró el mandatario. Además de beber y escuchar música, algunos asaltantes habrían cambiado su vestuario con pantalones y camisetas del propio almacén. Aunque retiraron las etiquetas visibles de precio, las autoridades aseguraron que los tickets seguían adheridos al interior de las prendas cuando se produjo la captura. Pese a que los captores intentaron proyectar una imagen intimidante —con pasamontañas, chalecos antibalas y armas que resultaron ser traumáticas—, las autoridades concluyeron que no se trataba de un grupo criminal altamente organizado. El alcalde los calificó como “mapuchines” y los describió como “rateros de poca monta” que pretendían “resolver el diciembre”. La expresión, usada en tono coloquial, buscaba subrayar que el grupo habría actuado con improvisación y falta de experiencia frente a un operativo de seguridad de esa magnitud.

articles.title: Phil Taylor: 16-time world champion and Adrian Lewis lose all five matches in return at pairs tournament
articles.summary: Phil Taylor and his England team-mate Adrian Lewis lose all five matches, having returned to darts action together at the MODUS Super Series International Pairs tournament.
articles.body:
Phil Taylor and his England team-mate Adrian Lewis lost all five matches as the pair returned to darts action together at the MODUS Super Series International Pairs tournament.

Taylor, a 16-time world champion, retired from senior-level darts in 2018, while Lewis has not competed on the PDC tour since 2023.

They signed for the tournament in Portsmouth after Taylor was tempted back by the prospect of playing alongside his long-term friend.

The 66-year-old landed his first dart at a double as he checked out on 84 but the duo went on to lose their opening match 4-3 against Scotland's John Henderson and Robert Thornton.

They subsequently suffered successive defeats to pairs from Sweden, Switzerland, Germany and Denmark.

The pair finished the night bottom of Group C, but will return to action on Friday for a second round-robin phase.

Taylor had not played competitively since the 2024 edition of World Seniors Darts Championship and was adamant the south-coast competition will be his last appearance at the tournament.

Speaking prior to his first match, he told Talksport , external : "This is the final time. It's got to be now. I've got all the things in my life now that I'm enjoying.

"I understand what Adrian's saying about travelling and being away. He's got a young family still, where my family have grown up, but I've still got grandkids.

"One stops and then another one begins again, life carries on. I enjoy being at home, that's the reason why I wouldn't be on the road again."

Taylor and two-time world champion Lewis, 41, won the World Cup of Darts four times together for England between 2012 and 2016.

Asked how his preparation for the tournament had gone, Taylor added: "For me, not very well, to be quite honest with you. I've lost it a little bit.

"Aidy, I know has been playing really well, so I'm going to be on his shoulders today. He's going to have to carry me a little bit."

articles.title: Brenden Dillon Suspended for Illegal Hit to Head, How Much Money Devils Star Loses Revealed
articles.summary: New Jersey Devils defenseman Brenden Dillon was suspended four games by the NHL on Thursday for his hit on Columbus Blue Jackets defenseman Denton Mateychuk during New Jersey's 3-2 win on Wednesday.
articles.body:
New Jersey Devils defenseman Brenden Dillon was suspended four games by the NHL on Thursday for his hit on Columbus Blue Jackets defenseman Denton Mateychuk during New Jersey's 3-2 win on Wednesday.

Per the Associated Press (h/t ESPN ), the NHL's department of player safety stated that Dillon executed a "high, hard check, elevating upward and unnecessarily and making Mateychuk's head the main point of contact on a hit where such head contact was avoidable."

Dillon was given a match penalty, which resulted in his ejection from the game. Mateychuk did not return to the game for Columbus after absorbing the high hit.

According to the AP (h/t ESPN), Dillon will lose $82,474.24 because of the suspension.

Blue Jackets head coach Rick Bowness gave a positive update Wednesday on Mateychuk, telling reporters that the blueliner "feels fine," before adding "protocol will take over and we'll go from there."

Dillon, 36, is in the midst of his 16th NHL season and his third as a member of the Devils.

Over 1,072 career regular-season games, Dillon has recorded 43 goals and 186 assists for 229 points to go along with a plus-62 rating and 1,051 penalty minutes.

Through 16 games this season, the former Dallas Stars, San Jose Sharks, Washington Capitals and Winnipeg Jets rearguard has registered one goal, one assist, 37 penalty minutes and a plus-1 rating.

The 22-year-old Mateychuk was the 12th overall pick by Columbus in the 2022 NHL draft.

He set career highs last season with 13 goals and 18 assists for 31 points, and in 22 games so far this season, Mateychuk has delivered four goals and three assists for seven points to go along with a minus-4 rating.

The Devils, who are second in the Eastern Conference's Metropolitan Division with 34 points, will be without Dillon for games against the Calgary Flames, Jets, Sharks and Ottawa Senators.

Dillon will be eligible to return when New Jersey goes on the road to face the Pittsburgh Penguins on Dec. 5.

articles.title: MAC admits that officials incorrectly cost Kent State touchdown with blown call against Eastern Michigan
articles.summary: The Mid-American Conference admitted officials erred overturning Kent State's touchdown against Eastern Michigan, citing insufficient video evidence.
articles.body: Officiating in college football has become a major, major problem. Earlier this season, the Michigan Wolverines miraculously escaped against Western Michigan thanks to a controversial second being added to the game clock due to incorrect replay review procedures. While the MAC initially accepted the results, they then issued a statement criticizing how the situation was handled. The Big 12 Conference admitted to several officiating mistakes, most of which benefited the BYU Cougars. During their game against Notre Dame, the referees failed to notice that the Irish should have had one second left to try and pull off a comeback win. CLOCK CONTROVERSY: NCAA SAYS OFFICIALS BOTCHED REPLAY PROTOCOL IN MICHIGAN'S WIN OVER WESTERN MICHIGAN "Following the Big 12's review of the final play of Saturday's Notre Dame-BYU game, it was determined that time remained on the clock when the ball hit the ground and the play was incorrectly cleared by the replay officiating crew," they explained in a statement. "The Conference will conduct a complete review of its end-of-game officiating process in advance of next week's games." Then there was the inexplicable handling of the end of the BYU-UCF game, where a facemask penalty flag was picked up, and the Knights were incorrectly assessed a 10-second runoff at the end of regulation. Amazingly, the next week, the Cougars were given a touchdown on a fumble recovery that should not have been allowed thanks to a blown whistle. In the SEC, the Texas-Missouri game featured several contentious calls that went the Longhorns' way, including the most absurd, awarding Arch Manning and Texas a first down on a fumble, though his arm was clearly moving forward. Analysts were so critical of the officiating in that game that they drew a rebuke from Greg Sankey afterward. Notre Dame-Miami came down to what looked to be a massive touchdown catch for the Irish, waved off as incomplete. Those are just a few examples. And now we have another one. This time, ironically, involving MAC officials. CLICK HERE FOR MORE OUTKICK SPORTS COVERAGE During some recent late-night MACtion, a Kent State appeared to come down with a walk-off touchdown catch to beat Eastern Michigan. After an insane five-minute review process, the officials overturned it, based on, well, not much, and handed the win to the Eagles. THE ABSOLUTE WORST CALL OF THE COLLEGE FOOTBALL SEASON HAPPENED LAST NIGHT WHILE YOU WERE SLEEPING On Wednesday, the conference admitted that the officials erred in making the call and that Kent State should have won the game. In a statement, they acknowledged that there was "insufficient video evidence to overturn the ruling on the field." "The video evidence did not meet the clear and obvious standard required to overturn the ruling on the field," they added. "The decision to overturn the touchdown was incorrect, and the original ruling should have been upheld. The Mid-American Conference recognizes the significance of this error and regrets its impact on the outcome of the game. Our student-athletes, coaches, institutions and fans deserve the highest standards of officiating. The Conference remains committed to those standards and to maintaining the competitive integrity of our contests." "Heartbroken for our players and staff who pour so much of themselves into what we do - especially those playing their last game of college football. We are extremely proud of the way our young men represent Kent State, our football program, and themselves." Man, it doesn't get worse than that. Having the outcome of a game be directly affected by the officials making the wrong ruling. You have to feel terrible for Kent State players, fans, and coaches. And frustrating that officiating continues to be such a disaster when there's no excuse for it to be. Gotta be better and let the MACtion dictate the outcome, not the refs.

articles.title: No. 2 ‘Iolani stifles No. 5 Mililani in boys basketball
articles.summary: Even this early in nonconference play, tough competition has already sharpened the ‘Iolani Raiders. Eight days after opening with an overtime loss to No. 1 K...
articles.body:
Even this early in nonconference play, tough competition has already sharpened the 'Iolani Raiders.

Eight days after opening with an overtime loss to No. 1 Kahuku, No. 2 'Iolani used stifling defense to post a 49-37 boys basketball win over No. 5 Mililani on Wednesday night at Father Bray Athletic Center. Declan Beckette paced the Raiders (2-1) with 17 points despite early foul trouble.

Raymon Teocson stepped up with 16 points, scoring from mid-range and in the paint as 'Iolani opened an early double-digit lead and retained it despite tough man-to-man defense by the Trojans in the second half.

"I think there's been a lot of growth from fall season and three weeks in the season now," Beckette said. "One thing we've struggled with is injuries. Casey (Lee) is a big energy guy for us, he hurt his ACL. Kahua (Benton) messed up his wrist during the Leilehua game. He went up for a block and landed on it. Those are some important guys. The goal is just to make the little improvements every day."

Ambrose Smith, a 6-foot-5 senior, hustled for nine points. A year ago, he was a more of a volleyball guy who provided a lot of energy on the basketball court. Now, he's evolving into a scorer on the block in addition to his penchant for rebounding.

"We all know what everyone does well and what everyone can do to improve," Beckette said.

Tui Tukimaka finished with 14 points to lead Mililani (4-1). The Trojans posted home wins over Damien, Waipahu and Mid-Pacific before going on the road to battle the Raiders.

"I like the fact that this team can get better," Mililani coach Garrett Gabriel said. "We have a lot of players and it's putting the pieces of the puzzle together. It's going to take some time. We played a really good ILH team. You've got to be at your best. The first quarter hurt us the most. We didn't hit any shots and they did, but overall, it was good. You learn a lot."

Mililani's next game is a week from today at Na Koa Invitational, a Kamehameha boys basketball tournament. The Trojans open against host Kamehameha. 'Iolani's next game is next Wednesday at home against Moanalua.

The first few minutes had a very athletic, physical tone, but officials were consistent with calling illegal screens. Each team was whistled for two in the first three minutes.

'Iolani got two pull-up 3-point jumpers from Beckette to open a 12-4 lead. However, the 6-foot-3 sharpshooter picked up his second foul with less than 2 minutes left in the first quarter and sat down. The Raiders kept rolling. La'a Bumalag drove and dished to Kiai Kam for a long 2 at the buzzer, opening 'Iolani's lead to 16-4 going into the second quarter.

Beckette picked up his third foul with 1:27 left in the first half, joining three other Raiders and Trojans in total who had the same burden. 'Iolani led 27-18 at intermission.

A corner 3 by Micah Lile opened the home team's lead to 30-18 to open the second half.

Mililani stayed in range, pulling within 40-33 early in the fourth quarter with tough defense. However, Beckette scored back-to-back buckets. His baseline drive against tough defense opened the lead to 44-33 with 4 minutes remaining.

articles.title: D-I, D-II titles up for grabs, featuring Waipahu, 2 Kauai teams, KS-Maui
articles.summary: Kapolei’s triumphant finish, a first-ever state football championship for the school and guru Darren Hernandez, makes everything that follows anti-climactic....
articles.body:
Kapolei's triumphant finish, a first-ever state football championship for the school and guru Darren Hernandez, makes everything that follows anti-climactic.

Maybe. On paper, it's hard to top history in the Open Division. On the field, Waipahu and Kapaa will provide a fascinating, raw-boned clash of run-first teams with a history of explosive aerial playmakers. The Division I final in the Hawaii Army National Guard/HHSAA Football State Championships could be is an extension of the Open, where seven-day-a-week football players who never stop training gravitate to coaches and friends in a process that creates consolidation.

The D-II state final is still grassroots at heart. Waimea football is in its niche in this division, a proud history providing the foundation. Generations of players who become coaches, teaching the same fundamentals that propelled Waimea to the big stage. Kamehameha-Maui is back to defend its D-II state title, a program that is small in numbers but stacked with some of the best athletes in Maui County.

Saturday, 7:30 p.m., John Kauinana Stadium

Long ago, in a galaxy known as 94 Block, a young coach poured his mind, heart, soul, time and energy into his family.

All Bryson Carvalho did was grind. So his assistants and players followed suit. Walking the walk is all they have done in the years since he accepted the position as head coach of the Waipahu Marauders. He brought a twist and a golden flavor. The kids want a huge pre-game intro? Bring it on. The black flag? It stays, but we don the top of the bleachers at Masa Yonamine Athletic Complex with blue and gold Waipahu flags.

Every day, the staff honors a hard-working player as their Marauder of the Day. The mega-faux gold WWE-era championship belt is strapped on and the potentially corny idea has become a genuine tradition embraced throughout the program, through the years.

Waipahu's stampede through the OIA Division I season was no surprise. All the grit and scrappiness of any program is a must, but there are no weight classes on the gridiron. Waipahu (12-1) had a talented offensive line by D-I standards, but when transfers began to bolster the trenches three years ago, the dream expanded.

This front five of LT Urijah Saifoloi (6-2, 275), LG Andrew Fruean (6-3, 350), C Peyton Taumua (6-0, 302), RG Josiah Tuatagaloa (6-3, 345) and RT Pierce Taumua (6-1, 305) is possibly the biggest in state history with the skill to match.

When Waipahu opened the season with defending Open Division state champion Campbell, two truths materialized. One, the Sabers were depleted defensively by graduation, but the work would come and restore order. Two, Waipahu didn't care who you were or what your classification is.

That night, the Marauders didn't necessarily gash Campbell's defense. Carvalho and his staff made a point: we will run, we will achieve our objectives, we will make your defense stay on the field. Waipahu ran the ball 37 times for 151 yards.

It was far from perfect, but it was a perfect mindset and tone setter. Waipahu led 40-10 with 3:39 left and walked off the field with a 40-17 win. A week later, Kapolei showed what a legendary defense does, shutting down Waipahu, 50-15. The Marauders felt that sting for a day, went back to work and took out that anguish on the rest of the state.

The three-headed backfield lost Elias Mahuka later to injury, and sneakily explosive Rocco Silofau returned from injury in November. Senior Tristan Pacheco (1,383 yards, 22 TDs) is making a run like few other Marauder RBs. Sophomore QB Jake Garcia (2,883 yards, 31 TDs, four interceptions) has been masterful in and out of the pocket (six rushing TDs).

WR Jayse Braun (63 receptions, 1,434 yards, 19 TDs) still gets tested by single coverage, still keeps beating cornerbacks deep.

Kapaa (6-1-1) has the athleticism, size and schematics to keep Braun from getting loose. Can the Warriors contain both without allowing WRs Lyric Anuenue and Ian Tutuvanu to control the middle of the field?

Kapaa's offense resembles the four-wide packages that love to ground and pound.

The Warriors line up with LT Tavyn Boiser (5-9, 210), LG Elias Muli (5-11, 220), C Dwayne Padre-Kusaka (5-8, 200), RG Kaiona Manantan (6-0, 250) and RT Bobby Kaneakua (6-0, 280). Kaneakua has also played center. Versatile sophomore Kahuwila Kanakaole (6-2, 215) has lined up as an eligible lineman at tight end in Kapaa's unbalanced line.

Coach Ryan "Mack" McKeague has stuck to the blueprint set by former coach Mike Tresler, who still helps the team out.

"I'm an understudy of Mike Tresler and our whole staff is," McKeague said of the former UH defensive back. "We stay in bedrock and try to stay basic with fundamentals."

Kapaa won the D-I state title in 2024, edging Konawaena, 10-7. Last year, the Warriors lost to Kailua in the final, 13-9. After years of coming close in D-II, they are officially a D-I powerhouse. This program would be competitive in Open Division and with a little more depth, possibly contend there.

Waipahu won the D-I state title in 2018 under Carvalho, and won again in '23. The past two seasons were in the Open Division. It's very debatable whether Waipahu has simply outgrown D-I.

"Waipahu is no joke," McKeague said. "We know they'll get after it."

No. 10 (1) Kamehameha-Maui (8-2) vs. (2) Waimea

KS-Maui has dominated the MIL in recent seasons, beating D-I and D-II foes alike. This year, longtime coach Ulima Afoa's team saw three players transfer to Kapalama with the chance to play in the Open Division. The Warriors kept trucking, and a 16-6 loss to eventual MIL D-I champion Baldwin was the only 'L' on the ledger.

The Warriors (8-2) aren't immune from some natural, built-in envy. Like KS-Hawaii, KS-Maui draws talented student-athletes from across the county, including smaller schools that cringe at the thought of losing born-and-bred hometown talent. In the end, almost nobody says no to the opportunity to graduate with the name of the Princess on that diploma.

Kaikea Hueu, Nakoa Pau, Bruce Beltran, Kukauakuewa So'o are the latest edition of Warriors who live by their actions. They stayed put and kept the fire going at Kana'iaupuni Stadium.

"The kids have done a nice job of keeping it together. They had a heck of a game this past week," Afoa said, referring to a 29-11 semifinal win over previously unbeaten Kalaheo. KS-Maui's offensive line has set the tone all season.

LT So'o (6-1, 275), LG Kalewa Pascua (6-0, 305), C Jeremiah Kea (5-5, 200), RG Lhyam Cremer (5-6, 215) and RT Kahualii Piena (6-1, 245) have protected QB Ryder DeSilva (12 TDs, two interceptions) and paved the way for RB Xander Pagan (792 yards, 11 TDs).

Defensively, Elai Mossman (6-2, 230), Pau (5-6, 200) and Kapena Lani (6-1, 170) are in the trenches. Lani had 8.5 tackles against Kalaheo while Pau, also listed as a RB, had two sacks.

The linebacking corps includes Hueu (5-10, 195), who scored on a fumble return against Kalaheo. Hueu has also been a playmaker at RB over his career.

Isaac Gosselin (6-1, 190) and Josiah Kaya-Medeiros (6-1, 190) round out the senior crew at LB.

The Warriors' secondary includes S Uriah Sardine and cornerbacks Nohi Casco, Kaimana Carrizosa and Kai'kena Gusman.

At Waimea (4-5), there is no consolidation of talent from a greater area. The Menehune are who they are and have been for generations, going back to Coach Adam Rita, and then Jon Kobayashi. Kyle Linoz coaches the JPS program and, like a fantastic educator who teaches a subject and trains students after school in debate or robotics or marching band, has a staff that preaches fundamentals to the nth degree.

Waimea won the D-II state crown for a first time in 2022, routing King Kekaulike, 45-6. In '23, they repeated with a 31-28 thriller over KS-Maui.

Waimea returns a vast number of key players from last year's sophomore-heavy roster. If the Menehune are overlooked, they are just used to it.

That loss at KS-Hawaii on Aug. 21 produced heartbreak. Starting QB Kolby Correa suffered a season-ending injury. The blueprint for the 2026 Waimea offense was overhauled.

"We had to revamp our offense, getting to a different style from what we had practiced," Linoz said. "We were going to throw it a lot more. Now we're back to three yards and a cloud of dust."

They've made it work with two QBs: Paka Cintron-Chandler and Chance Gomes. Both are seniors. Cintron-Chandler is still listed as a RB. Waimea had already lost WR/DB Nash Schaefer to a collarbone injury in a scrimmage before the KS-Hawaii trip.

Everything settled in gradually behind the cornerstone of Waimea's offensive line. LT Henry Kanahele IV (6-1, 210), LG Kama Kahea Jr. (5-9, 260), C Xyrus Bajo (6-1, 330), RG Micah Linnell (5-11, 290) and RT Samson Kaohelaulii-Kala (6-5, 250) had spent months preparing as pass protectors. Since Correa's injury, they are the core of Waimea's survival and success, facing stacked boxes and churning out a small win on every four-yard gain.

Waimea's defense doesn't have the luxury of size. None of the O-linemen double up on defense.

"Our D-line averages about 155 pounds," Linoz said. "They're fast, though. We let our little guys just nip at their ankles all game. They played against Kapaa all year so they know how to play the big dudes."

NG Makai Calvin (5-9, 160) and LB Cyler Aranio (5-10, 165) can rely on technique and angles against bigger foes in the trenches. Aranio and LB Kana'i Huihui-Caberto do the diagnosis on field.

Waimea's kicking game relies on placement more than sheer leg power. Junior Wade Silva could be an x-factor.

articles.title: Cumberland's wildcat gamble paid off with a Thanksgiving rivalry win
articles.summary: Izik Supple took on a new role, then changed Cumberland's rivalry game with a 29-12 win over Woonsockey.
articles.body:
WOONSOCKET – Cumberland served up a little something different to go along with the standard rivalry football menu on this Thanksgiving .

The Clippers broke out a wildcat package on offense, and Izik Supple feasted in the second half while running past Woonsocket.

Supple rushed for 168 yards and two touchdowns as Cumberland surged to a 29-12 victory over the Villa Novans on a gray, breezy morning at Dionne Track. The Clippers ripped off 22 unanswered points after halftime, including scoring dashes of 34 yards and 80 yards from their junior captain.

"We weren't pushing the ball," Supple said. "Our defense was hanging in there, but we needed to make a change."

Cumberland erased a 12-7 deficit out of the locker room with a sharp drive to open the third quarter. Supple went up the middle to convert on a fourth down at his own 31 and carried on each of the last five plays to find the end zone. He broke up the middle and cut toward the right hash with 6:14 left to make it a 15-12 game.

"My immediate reaction was, 'Let's do this,'" Supple said. "I was excited. I love having that responsibility."

The Clippers added on later in the quarter when Woonsocket fumbled out by midfield. Declan Jones scooped it up and was loose, rumbling 45 yards for a score that made it 22-12. It was a second defensive touchdown of the day for Cumberland, as Jones followed a fumble return from the same distance by Ethan Delgado Rolland early in the second quarter that put the Clippers on the board.

"Every day we tell ourselves we're the best run defense in the state," Supple said. "We believe it."

The Villa Novans missed a 38-yard field goal with 7:31 left in the fourth, and Supple added the finishing touch on the next play. He went untouched through the left side and broke into the open, sprinting into the freshening wind and crossing the goal line ahead of Woonsocket's pursuit off the right side. Zack Deroy's extra point made it a three-score game and all but sealed it.

"That might be the longest 80 yards I've ever seen in my life," Supple said. "It felt like I was running for 10 years."

Cumberland (4-6) had dropped two of the last three meetings on the holiday, including a 9-7 setback at home last year. The Clippers snapped a three-game losing streak with a 22-21 road win at Norwood (Mass.) last week and built some confidence into this one. They now hold a 38-20-4 advantage in a series dating to 1964.

"This victory, it feels so amazing," Supple said. "It's so special."

Carlos Valentin's 63-yard touchdown run and Armani Cepeda's 38-yard scoring reception from Jalil Quinones-Diaz both came in the second quarter and gave the Villa Novans (4-6) a lead into halftime. Quinones-Diaz left with 38 seconds remaining due to an apparent neck injury, with emergency medical personnel tending to him and transporting him to a local hospital. Quinones-Diaz had movement in his extremities, opening both arms and waving to teammates as he was loaded into a waiting ambulance.

C – Ethan Delagdo Rolland 45 fumble recovery (Zack Deroy kick)

W – Carlos Valentin 63 run (kick failed)

W – Armani Cepeda 38 pass from Jalil Quinones-Diaz (rush failed)

C – Declan Jones 45 fumble recovery (Deroy kick)

articles.title: Tirarán de la manta del 'Sandpapergate', la trampa del papel de lija que avergonzó al deporte
articles.standfirst: Cricket Australia hará públicas las conclusiones de la investigación sobre 'Sandpapergate'
articles.summary: Cricket Australia hará públicas las conclusiones de la investigación sobre 'Sandpapergate'
articles.body: Cricket Australia anunció que hará públicas las conclusiones de una investigación independiente sobre el denominado 'Sandpapergate', el escándalo del papel de lija que sacudió al críquet australiano durante la gira por Sudáfrica de 2018, aunque no contempla la imposición de nuevas sanciones a los implicados. La investigación estará dirigida por Fiona McLeod, abogada especializada, quien encabezará un foro independiente encargado de escuchar los testimonios de los jugadores y miembros del equipo técnico que participaron en aquella gira, así como de los directivos y responsables de la federación nacional en ese momento. La iniciativa también examinará las prácticas relacionadas con el mantenimiento y manipulación de la pelota durante toda la temporada 2017-2018, incluidos los cuatro partidos de prueba disputados en territorio sudafricano. El caso estalló en marzo de 2018, cuando las cámaras captaron al entonces jugador australiano Cameron Bancroft ocultando un trozo de papel de lija durante un encuentro contra Sudáfrica, en una acción destinada a alterar las condiciones de la pelota y obtener una ventaja deportiva. El episodio provocó una de las mayores crisis de reputación del críquet australiano y derivó en una investigación interna y sanciones contra varios integrantes del equipo, entre ellos el entonces capitán Steve Smith, el vicecapitán David Warner y el propio Bancroft. El presidente interino de Cricket Australia, David Boon, explicó que el nuevo foro pretende ofrecer un espacio seguro para que los participantes puedan relatar sus versiones de los acontecimientos y aportar información sobre la gira y la investigación posterior. Boon reconoció también el impacto que la renovada atención sobre aquel episodio ha tenido en las personas involucradas y aseguró que su bienestar constituye una prioridad para la organización. El foro tendrá una duración de seis semanas y no obligará a declarar a los antiguos jugadores y responsables que no deseen participar, aunque McLeod podrá convocar a otras personas si lo considera necesario. Cricket Australia se comprometió a publicar íntegramente el informe y emitir una respuesta dentro de los 30 días posteriores a su recepción

articles.summary: LUCKNOW: Defending champions Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand advanced to the women’s doubles quarterfinals with a straight-games win while second seed
articles.body: LUCKNOW: Defending champions Treesa Jolly and Gayatri Gopichand advanced to the women’s doubles quarterfinals with a straight-games win while second seed Tanvi Sharma rallied from a game down to reach the women’s singles quarterfinals at the Syed Modi India International Super 300 on Thursday.Treesa and Gayatri beat Shreya Balaji and Pranavi Natarajan 21-9, 21-8. Tanvi beat Indonesia’s Mutiara Ayu Puspitasari 18-21, 21-18, 21-18 in 68 minutes.Unnati Hooda defeated American Ishika Jaiswal 21-14, 21-18 while Tasnim Mir upset Scotland’s sixth seed Kirsty Gilmour 21-19, 21-15.Anmol Kharb completed the Indian women’s singles quartet by beating compatriot and fifth seed Ashmita Chaliha 21-16, 2115.“I don’t think I played my best today,” Tanvi said. India’s Dhruv Kapila and Tanisha Crasto, the mixed doubles top seeds, lost 20-22, 15-21 to Malaysia’s Wee Yee Hern and Vannee Gobi.Viraj Kuvale and Rutaparna Panda came from behind to win their mixed doubles match against Gregoire Deschamp and Iben Bergstein 16-21, 21-13, 21-17.Sathwik Reddy Kanapuram and Reshika Uthayasooriyan also progressed In men’s singles, Tushar Suveer beat qualifier Shashwat Dalal 21-14, 21-12. Third seeds Hariharan Amsakarunan and MR Arjun advanced in men’s doubles.Get the latest Sports News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: India’s Pant plays for New Zealand side under false name ‘Stan Stan’
articles.summary: Rishabh Pant plays for Open House Swingers in New Zealand on eve of second Test as India wicketkeeper uses false name.
articles.body:
India’s star wicketkeeper-batsman Rishabh Pant used an unlikely forum to keep his eye sharp before the second New Zealand Test – a social Last Man Stands match in Christchurch.

The 29-year-old, who plays for Lucknow Super Giants in the Indian Premier League, is one of the six most prolific hitters in Test history, hitting 108 across his 53 matches to sit second all time.

Six of those came in Wellington last week, where his 128 from 153 balls helped India set a record in New Zealand, 720-9 in the drawn match.

After a chance encounter in central Christchurch, Pant played Wednesday for the Open House Swingers in a Last Man Stands match against The Chosen Ones at Hagley Park – not to be confused with neighbouring Hagley Oval, where Pant will wear Indian whites this week.

Listed on the scorecard as Stan Stan, Pant blasted 54 from 21 balls to maintain his glittering form in New Zealand.

“I saw Rishabh going around on an electric bike,” Open House Swingers player Mohammad Safi told the New Zealand Herald.

“So I went and stopped him, and we start talking and taking a few photos and stuff, and I asked him, do you want to play cricket for us?

“He was like, OK, I’ll come and play for you guys. Then he came and padded up, went batting, and smashed a few sixes.”

Indian bowling coach Morne Morkel said he “nearly fell off my chair last night when I saw that”.

New Zealand captain Tom Latham said Pant’s midweek performance was “brilliant”.

“He’s obviously a real character of the game is Rishabh, so it’s great for him to give his experience back to the LMS teams.”

Safi told the New Zealand Herald the opposition did not recognise Pant while he wore his striking blue tracksuit.

Safi also said Pant used his cousin’s bat during the match.

“He was asking me to basically give him a single and stuff. Obviously, I was smashing longer sixes than him, and then he was like, give me a turn, let me show you how to hit it,” Safi said.

The Open House Swingers won the match by 16 runs, a feat Pant could not achieve in Wellington, as the Test ended in a draw.

India’s second Test against New Zealand begins Friday at Hagley Oval.
