articles.title: Messi confirms Tevez testimonial as Ronaldo showdown in offing
articles.summary: Argentina footballer Lionel Messi confirms testimonial game for Carlos Tevez, with Cristiano Ronaldo role also sought.
articles.body:
Lionel Messi will play in ⁠former ⁠Argentina teammate Carlos Tevez’s testimonial match on December 20, organisers ⁠have confirmed.

Tevez, nicknamed “Apache”, retired in 2022, bringing the curtain down ⁠on a career that included stints at Manchester City, Manchester United and Juventus.

The 42-year-old, who ended his ‌career at boyhood club Boca Juniors, said last year he wanted Messi and former Manchester United teammate Cristiano Ronaldo to play in opposing teams ⁠in his testimonial.

“It will ⁠be a true honour to welcome the best player in the world to ⁠Apache’s last dance,” organisers posted on Instagram ⁠on Thursday.

Rio Ferdinand, ⁠Sergio Aguero, Leandro Paredes, Gianluigi Buffon and Martin Palermo are among the other players ‌confirmed for the match, which will take place at Boca ‌Juniors’ ‌La Bombonera stadium.

Messi and Ronaldo last faced each other in a competitive match in 2020 when representing Barcelona and Juventus, respectively.

The pair also played in an exhibition match when Messi’s Paris Saint-Germain faced a Riyadh Season XI in 2023 following Ronaldo’s move to the Saudi Pro League.

Messi and Inter Miami to dig deep in MLS at Columbus

Meanwhile, with the season and defence of ‌the MLS Cup title on the line, Inter Miami coach Cristian “Kily” Gonzalez believes ⁠in his players heading ⁠into Game 2 of the best-of-three Eastern Conference series at the Columbus Crew on Friday.

“There are moments when you have to dig deep, tap ⁠into that sense of self-respect and the passion that drives you,” he told the media in Spanish on Wednesday. “That’s how I see the game, and I truly hope ⁠we can demonstrate that this Friday.”

The No 2 seed Herons have no choice after a 3-0 home loss to the No 7 Crew on Saturday has them facing a first-round exit for the second time in three seasons.

Game 3, if necessary, will be on Wednesday in Miami.

Miami will receive ‌a cold reception in Columbus not only because of a forecasted temperature in the upper 30s with a chance of snow flurries.

During the Crew’s 2-1 win on September 27, Miami was issued five of the nine yellow cards and the lone red card.

On a throw-in during Game 1, Lionel Messi threw the ball into the face of Gonzalo Tapia. Both received cautions.

Crew interim coach Laurent Courtois felt Messi deserved ⁠more than a yellow card.

“There’s multiple ways to see that (situation),” Courtois ⁠said on Monday. “If you talk about purely the soccer part, I think when he dove inside of our box [earlier in the game], it should’ve been a yellow to start with. And this incident is not only ⁠the [throw-in]. It’s the whole sequence that leads to it, and you can tell that there’s weird intentions at the least, so it ⁠is what it is.”

There were 36 fouls on Saturday – 22 ⁠by Miami – and the Herons had five yellows and one damning red card.

After Tapia put the Crew ahead 1-0 on a penalty kick in the ninth minute, Gonzalo Lujan picked up his second yellow in the 36th ‌and the Crew got goals from Taha Habroune (52nd) and Tapia (58th). Lujan is suspended for Friday’s match.

“I believe the squad are at a point where we understand that it’s time to deliver,” ‌Miami ‌forward Luis Suarez said. “This is our final opportunity. This format has given us another chance to play this Friday, and it’s the last shot we have to bring the series back home.”

articles.title: Ronnie O'Sullivan: Seven-time world snooker champion open to entering qualifiers for Crucible showpiece
articles.summary: Ronnie O'Sullivan exclusively reveals to Sky Sports that he would be open to entering qualifiers for the World Championship should he be outside the top 16 in April; In a wide-ranging interview, O'Sullivan also reflected on his recent poor form and the Crucible's renovation
articles.body:
O'Sullivan is currently 13th in the world rankings - with only the top 16 guaranteed an automatic place at the showpiece event in Sheffield - and has endured a challenging start to the season, losing in the first round of each of his last four tournaments.

'The Rocket' has previously asserted that he would rather retire than have to play qualifiers, having set himself a deadline of 2028 to win his eighth world title before retiring - but, in an exclusive interview, the 50-year-old has revealed he is beginning to warm to the idea of a different path to the Crucible.

"Everything's going against me [in terms of qualification]," O'Sullivan told Sky Sports.

"My main aim this year is to try and get enough points to not have to qualify, because I probably will drop outside the top 16.

"I've been making a few phone calls to a lot of the other players, asking: 'what's it like down at the qualifiers? When you play this tournament, how many matches did you play?'

"I'm already sort of getting ready for [qualifying], to be honest with you.

"I'm not filled with a lot of confidence, but I think it's better to be a realist rather than someone that's a bit of a dreamer."

O'Sullivan is frank about where his recent poor form could leave him in the rankings, but maintains the pivotal factor in his participation will be his enjoyment of the sport, rather than his route to the tournament.

"If I'm enjoying playing, I'll go and play the qualifiers. If I'm not, then I'll just stay somewhere else and enjoy life, you know?

"But for me to go there or to go anywhere, I've got to really feel like I'm enjoying playing.

"Hopefully I can be in a good place with my game - I don't mind a little trip to Leicester for a week or so!"

O'Sullivan faces a qualifier in the first round of the UK Championship on Sunday, and will be looking to end his barren run of form - most recently including a loss to 61-year-old Tony Drago at the Snooker 900 Crucible Cup - in the first triple-crown event of the season.

He last won the event in 2023, his ninth win at the York Barbican, and has dropped seven places in the seeding after entering the 2025 edition as the sixth seed.

"I don't really expect too much - I just have to go there and just see what happens, really," O'Sullivan added. "I don't think the seeding matters much.

"In 2012, when I won the World Championship, I was fortunate to not have to qualify that year, but then I was playing better, you know? It's probably a slightly different situation now, you know, 14 years on.

"My form's not as good as it was then, and the standard is a lot better now than it was then."

When asked if he was still enjoying playing, O'Sullivan replied: "I am! But you've still got to get rid of a few matches.

"The last three tournaments I've entered, I've got beaten first round, so that's not good.

"It'd be nice to win a few matches, you know, just to give yourself a little bit of a boost.

"I'm putting the work in on the practice table. So if you're getting pumped first round every time, it's not a good feeling."

O'Sullivan: World Championship isn't as difficult to win as most think

The seven-time world champion is the first to admit a tournament win seems a fair distance from his recent travails, but thinks that his poor form could be the less worrying at the Crucible than in shorter events, like the upcoming UK Championship.

"The World Championship - in some ways - is not as difficult to win as a lot of the other events," O'Sullivan added.

"It's such a long event - it's one of those that you can come into it not playing great.

"I've always found over the years that there's a lot of players that have won it - and they've had horrific seasons, had no form, and then do well in it.

"If I beat John Higgins [in the 2025 quarter-final] I'd have fancied my chances against Murphy in the semis. I was only one frame away.

"It's always fine lines, but it's not as difficult at all to win as most people probably think."

O'Sullivan self-induced deadline of 2028 to win the World Championship falls before its iconic venue, the Crucible, is set to undergo a £45m renovation in 2029 and 2030.

The redevelopment means the tournament will be moved for the first time since 1977, with O'Sullivan speculating that the highlight of the snooker calendar may even leave British shores for the first time.

"I think [moving it out of the UK] is a reality now," he added. "They're definitely going to take it somewhere else.

"It's a lot of money to spend for an extra 500 seats. Hopefully it makes it a big difference, but you can get a lot for £45m. Hopefully they do a really good job on it."

articles.title: David Sánchez, sobre la situación del Getafe: "El último milagro de José Bordalás fue el de la temporada pasada"
articles.standfirst: El presentador de Despierta San Francisco analiza en La Tribu la crisis del conjunto azulón y reivindica la figura de su entrenador
articles.summary: El presentador de Despierta San Francisco analiza en La Tribu la crisis del conjunto azulón y reivindica la figura de su entrenador
articles.body: La situación del Getafe y su nuevo tropiezo europeo han centrado la opinión de David Sánchez en La Tribu de Radio MARCA. El periodista ha reflexionado sobre el momento que atraviesa el conjunto azulón y ha salido en defensa de José Bordalás, al que considera el principal responsable de los éxitos del equipo durante las últimas temporadas. "No hay milagros eternos y por eso da la sensación de que el último milagro de José Bordalás con el Getafe fue el de la temporada pasada", comenzó David Sánchez. El periodista puso en valor la capacidad del técnico alicantino para conseguir la permanencia del equipo e incluso llevarlo a competiciones europeas. Sin embargo, Sánchez considera que Bordalás se equivocó al continuar al frente del conjunto azulón. "Cometió solo un error, no dejar el Getafe la pasada temporada, sabiendo que tarde o temprano el equipo se la iba a pegar", afirmó. La defensa de Bordalás Tras lo que calificó como "otro ridículo europeo del equipo del sur de la capital", el periodista repartió responsabilidades entre todos los estamentos del club: "La culpa es de todo el mundo, de los que mandan, de los que juegan y de los que dirigen". Pese a la delicada situación del conjunto azulón, David Sánchez quiso reivindicar el legado del técnico: "Que nadie le quite ningún mérito a José Bordalás porque es, sin duda alguna, el mejor entrenador de la historia del Getafe". El periodista cerró su intervención con una reflexión sobre el final de una etapa de éxitos del conjunto madrileño: "Los milagros tienen fecha de caducidad y parece que la del Getafe caducó".

images.caption: Bordalás sentado en el banquillo en el partido contra el Atlético de Madrid
El técnico del Getafe se mostró crítico con la nueva derrota del conjunto azulón, aunque reconoció que la diferencia con el Atlético de Madrid "es abismal".

articles.title: Sandpapergate forum to investigate Australia-England Ashes Tests
articles.summary: Sandpapergate forum scope to cover entire 2017-18 season, including Ashes series, in South Africa allegations follow-up.
articles.body:
Cricket Australia (CA)’s forum into Sandpapergate will consider “ball-management practices” during the entire 2017-18 season, including the Ashes series, in the lead-up to the tour of South Africa, according to its ⁠terms of reference published on Friday.

The ball-tampering scandal was reignited this month after former Australia batter Usman Khawaja said the whole team had known about the cheating in South Africa, not just the three players found culpable by CA’s integrity unit.

CA announced ⁠on November 18 it would open an independent forum for players and staff to give their accounts of what happened in 2018 without fear of sanction.

The six-week forum, to be overseen by Australian barrister Fiona McLeod, will include all four tests of the 2018 South Africa tour but also extend to ball-management practices during the 2017-18 season.

That season included the five-test Ashes series, which Australia won 4-0. There ‌were no reports of Australia manipulating the ball illegally during the series.

The forum will also cover the conduct and scope of the 2018 integrity investigation, which found only three players culpable: Former captain Steve Smith and opening batters David Warner and Cameron Bancroft.

Smith and Warner were banned for 12 months, with Bancroft suspended for nine.

Khawaja’s former teammates Warner, Bancroft and Chadd Sayers have supported his comments that the wider playing group and staff were aware of the ball-tampering.

However, captain Pat Cummins and bowlers Mitchell Starc and Josh Hazlewood have strongly denied any prior knowledge.

CA backed Cummins to remain captain of the Test and ⁠one-day international sides last week and rejected any suggestion his integrity had been compromised amid the ⁠renewed furore.

McLeod will provide a report of findings from the forum to CA’s board but will not share the underlying accounts given by participants, the terms of reference said.

“This forum is the best opportunity for people to speak and be heard, and for CA to listen and ⁠learn,” CA Chair David Boon said in a statement.

Participation in the forum will be voluntary, and it will not make any adverse findings or determine the responsibility of any individual involved.

“Its purpose ⁠is to support the welfare of those impacted and to provide Participants with ⁠an opportunity to be heard and to have their experience acknowledged and understood without fear of retribution or disadvantage,” the terms said.

The Australian players’ union said it had not been consulted on developing the terms of reference.

“As such we don’t yet have a position on whether we support it and have advised ‌all relevant players of this as well as the fact that we are currently reviewing these terms and will update them once we have formed views,” Australian Cricketers’ Association boss Paul Marsh said in a statement.

Bancroft has said he will participate in the ‌forum, and former head coach Darren Lehmann told local media he would be open to it, saying he had nothing to hide.

Sayers said last week he was not sure whether he would participate, while Warner declined to confirm whether he would.

articles.title: This Bills keepsake captures 53 seasons of memories in Orchard Park
articles.summary: A new stadium means a new era. “Farewell to The Ralph” captures the games, fans and memories that defined the old one.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills have a new home, but the memories made at the old Highmark Stadium aren't going anywhere.

This holiday season, give the Bills fan in your life a keepsake celebrating more than five decades of unforgettable football, frigid Sundays and memories shared in Orchard Park.

"Farewell to The Ralph: Remembering Where We Cheered, Froze, Cried and Bonded" is a 208-page, premium-format coffee-table book celebrating the stadium the Bills called home for 53 seasons before moving into their new home across the parking lot.

Democrat and Chronicle Bills sportswriter Sal Maiorana's memories of watching games at the stadium dating back to his childhood.

D&C reporter Emily Barnes' look at the unique bond between the Bills and Western New York, through the winning years, the losing years and everything in between.

Dozens of memorable images from D&C photojournalists documenting the people, games and moments that defined the stadium.

Special coverage of the Bills' final game at their longtime home and the emotional farewell that closed one era before the franchise began another.

From the Bills' Super Bowl years of the early 1990s to Josh Allen's electrifying touchdown runs, the stadium provided the backdrop for generations of unforgettable moments. It was also where Bills fans shoveled snow, braved brutal cold and built traditions that became part of the identity of Western New York.

Now that the Bills have moved into their new stadium, "Farewell to The Ralph" preserves the stories, images and memories of the place they left behind.
authors: Democrat and Chronicle, Rochester Democrat and Chronicle

articles.title: El adiós de Alejandra Salazar está en manos de Gemma Triay
articles.standfirst: La leyenda cayó en octavos del Major de México y peligra su presencia en el Tour Finals de Barcelona: si Caldera y Goenaga vencen a Triay y Brea en cuartos habrá sido su último partido como profesional antes de retirarse
articles.summary: La leyenda cayó en octavos del Major de México y peligra su presencia en el Tour Finals de Barcelona: si Caldera y Goenaga vencen a Triay y Brea en cuartos habrá sido su último partido como profesional antes de retirarse
articles.body: Alejandra Salazar vive sus últimos partidos como profesional. La leyenda madrileña, que cuelga la pala a final de temporada, ha caído en octavos de final del México Major de Acapulco de Premier Padel y su presencia en el Tour Finals de Barcelona, último torneo del curso donde se reúnen las mejores 16 jugadoras del año, no está asegurada. Ella y Aranza Osoro cayeron en octavos ante Bea Caldera y Carmen Goenaga por 6-3 y 6-4, lo que provoca que, de ganar ambas hoy a las números 1 en cuartos de final, dejarían fuera a Alejandra. Es decir que, casualidades del destino -o no-, el adiós de Salazar antes de tiempo está en manos de Triay. Gemma y Delfi, cabe recordar, se están jugando el número 1. Por ránking y por lógica deberían avanzar y, de esta manera, asegurar de forma matemática que Alejandra esté en el Palau Sant Jordi para el torneo de maestras, pero la realidad es que Goenaga y Caldera ya han demostrado este año que pueden ganar a cualquiera. Un triunfo de Triay y Brea en semis aseguraría de forma matemática su segundo año consecutivo como reinas del pádel femenino y, de paso, la menorquina salvaría a su excompañera de una despedida 'prematura' antes de la gran fiesta final del pádel que albergará Barcelona.

articles.title: El Langui: "He priorizado la boccia a proyectos artísticos que llevaba años esperando"
articles.standfirst: El actor y rapero se ha colocado en el Top10 mundial en sólo un año compitiendo a nivel internacional. Ya no le da miedo decir que el objetivo es ir a los Juegos Paralímpicos de Los Ángeles 2028
articles.summary: El actor y rapero se ha colocado en el Top10 mundial en sólo un año compitiendo a nivel internacional. Ya no le da miedo decir que el objetivo es ir a los Juegos Paralímpicos de Los Ángeles 2028
articles.body: A Juan Manuel Montilla (Madrid, 1979), conocido como El Langui, le brillan los ojos y le sale la sonrisa al hablar de la boccia, el deporte paralímpico que descubrió hace dos años y que le ha cambiado la vida. En su primer año con la selección española ha ganado siete medallas internacionales (2 oros, 1 plata y 4 bronces), es tercero de Europa y décimo del mundo en BC1, categoría con limitaciones severas que afectan a piernas, brazos y tronco. Los dos Goyas y el MTV Europe Music Awards los tiene en casa de sus padres, pero las preseas deportivas las guarda en la suya. Le hacen sentir algo especial. Ya no tiene miedo a verbalizar que se ve con opciones de ir a los Juegos Paralímpicos de Los Ángeles 2028, una cita especial porque además es la cuna del rap, género en el que ha triunfado. PREGUNTA. ¿Cómo descubrió la boccia? RESPUESTA. Fue hace dos años a través de un mensaje que recibí de Raúl, más conocido como Champi en el mundo de la boccia. Es ex clasificador del Comité Paralímpico y Técnico de la Selección española. Me escribió para felicitarme por mis logros artísticos y me preguntó si hacía deporte. Cuando le dije que no empezó a meterme el gusanillo y a captarme. Fue el artífice de que yo esté haciendo boccia ahora. P. Su carrera ha sido meteórica. Este año sólo se le ha resistido el podio en el Mundial de Seúl. ¿Se imaginaba que llegaría tan lejos tan rápido? R. Cuando empecé no podía llegar a imaginar en el punto en el que estoy ahora. Siete medallas internacionales en mi primer año con la selección... Realmente empecé para desconectar de una obra de teatro, de un rodaje de cine o de un concierto. El primer año me lo tomé un poco así, de desconexión y para aprender la boccia. Pero claro, pasito a pasito fuimos ganando posiciones, ganando partidos, ganando la Liga, ganando la Copa de España, subcampeón del campeonato… Eso hizo que al final la mirada estuviera puesta en otros retos y que la selección española me convocara. P. Hace un año nos contó en su visita a MARCA que de niño soñaba con ser futbolista, pero que dejó el deporte de lado según se fue haciendo mayor porque parecía que no estaba hecho para usted por su discapacidad. ¿De alguna manera se ha quitado una espinita gracias a la boccia? R. Sí, yo creo que la boccia ha sacado esa espinita. Yo soñaba desde pequeño con ser futbolista y no pude cumplir mi sueño. Tuve que dejar el deporte porque jugaba al fútbol con mis amigos del colegio y del barrio que no tenían discapacidad y para jugar una pachanga estaba. Luego, al estar en los equipos de barrio de fútbol base, los entrenadores me decían: ‘Te puedes esperar en ese banco que estamos entrenando’. En los 80, el deporte paralímpico no tenía la visibilidad que tiene ahora. Probé el baloncesto en silla de ruedas, pero no tengo juego de hombro y no me veía. Desconecté del deporte y me enganché a la música y a lo que todo el mundo conoce. Estar ahora en el alto rendimiento compitiendo internacionalmente me he quitado esa espina. P. No sé si ha pensado alguna vez qué hubiera sido de ese niño si hubiese descubierto entonces la boccia. R. Me lo pregunto muchas veces y se lo digo también muchas veces a mi entrenador Juan Antonio y a Champi. ¿Por qué no me descubriste antes? ¿Por qué no me llamaste antes? Tengo 47 años, pero la boccia no tiene edad. Me hubiera encantado haber podido practicar deporte, haber podido entrar en el mundo de la boccia con 20 años. Mira la proyección que estamos viendo ahora, pues imagínate veinte años atrás. Hubiera disfrutado como un enano y hubiera intentado disputar Mundiales, Europeos a ir a varios Juegos Paralímpicos. P. ¿Cómo le ha cambiado la vida la boccia? R. Mira que hago cosas que me llenan de satisfacción, que me hacen sentir realizado y útil. Teatro, cine, música y proyectos muy bonitos. Pero cuando voy a competir a un torneo internacional tengo una sensación difícil de describir. Y cuando estoy en el podio con la medalla es una satisfacción muy diferente. Aunque he tenido reconocimiento dentro de la música, del cine, premios Goya, etc, cuando tienes una medalla sientes que eres tú quien ha lanzado esa bola, el que has tenido esa puntería y esa precisión. Tiene ese valor añadido que hace que tenga una satisfacción diferente. P. Al ser actor y cantante está acostumbrado a controlar los nervios para actuar ante mucha gente. ¿Su profesión le ayuda a gestionar mejor los nervios y la presión? R. Sí, me ha ayudado a controlar la presión en el terreno de juego. Estoy acostumbrado a salir a un escenario donde hay multitud de gente y a estar delante de una cámara y que digan ‘acción’. Tienes que hacerlo bien para no repetir muchas tomas, o en una obra de teatro salir en directo y soltarlo todo. Mi trabajo tiene ese punch añadido que hace que cuando llegue a un campeonato no esté tan nervioso y controle los nervios. P. Sigue actuando en el teatro, grabando series, también dirige y ahora es deportista. ¿De dónde saca tiempo para todo? R. La agenda es muy complicada. Estoy súper agradecido a los que hacen posible que yo pueda llegar a casi todo. Al final es el equipo que tienes detrás. En el mismo fin de semana te puede coincidir una obra de teatro con un rodaje y con una competición. Pero tengo mucha gente alrededor que está haciendo todo lo posible para que yo lo haga. P. ¿Le ha tocado renunciar a una actuación por la boccia? R. Sí, ya ha llegado ese momento en el que ha habido que priorizar la boccia a otros proyectos muy importantes de mi carrera y que llevaba mucho tiempo esperando. Si dejo de ir como internacional, quién sabe si podré llegar a unos Juegos Paralímpicos. Me he decantado por el deporte. P. Esas renuncias han dado sus frutos con esas siete medallas internacionales. ¿Cuál ha sido la clave de tu carrera meteórica? R. La clave es mi entrenador Juan Antonio López Mera, que ya ha estado en Juegos como técnico de boccia de la selección muchos años. Él es el artífice de optimizar los entrenamientos. Hay que echarle muchas horas y a veces yo no puedo echar tantas por mi trabajo. Entonces él sabe mis capacidades y hasta qué punto puedo llegar y en qué punto debo de estar yo para llegar a una competición y dar el 200%. Y súper agradecido también a Champi, que fue quien me descubrió este deporte y quien me puso a Juan Antonio. P. De las siete medallas internacionales, ¿con cuál se queda y por qué? R. Esta última plata de la Copa del Mundo en Brasil ha sido lo más porque ha sido mi primera final en una Copa del Mundo. Es la que más puntos me da para el ranking mundial pero la primera que gané en el Challenger de Olbia fue muy guay. Le tengo especial cariño. P. ¿Dónde guarda las medallas? R. Todos los premios de música, cine, televisión, etc. están en casa de mis padres y los deportivos, en una estantería de la mía. P. Este año ha disputado también su primer Mundial. ¿Cómo fue la experiencia? R. El Mundial fue algo que no me esperaba porque todavía no estaba en el ranking para llegar. Entré en el Mundial gracias al equipo español. No olvidemos que tenemos dos opciones para puntuar, ya que jugamos en individual y por equipos. Estaba en Seúl, en la Villa Olímpica, donde se habían disputado los Juegos. Estaba en esas instalaciones gigantescas con los mejores del mundo. Me tocó una pool complicada porque había dos asiáticos. Huadpradit, que tiene medallas paralímpicas, y el singapurense Jovin Tan, tercero del mundo. Fue una experiencia brutal y me quedó la espinita de ganar a Tan. Lo conseguí después en la semifinal de la Copa del Mundo de Sao Paulo. P. Precisamente en Brasil se celebraron los Juegos Paralímpicos de 2016 –en Río de Janeiro- en los que usted puso la música al equipo paralímpico español. Y ahora va camino de disputar usted unos Juegos. ¡Las vueltas que da la vida! R. La Copa del Mundo de Sao Paulo se celebró en el Centro de Alto Rendimiento Paralímpico Brasileño. Allí tienen un museo de los Juegos de Río y era curioso porque todos los días entraba y me acordaba de que en 2016 yo había hecho para el equipo español la canción ‘Se salen’. ¡Quién me diría a mí entonces, que conocí un montón de deportistas paralímpicos, que iba a estar yo aquí jugando con la selección P. Cuando vino a MARCA hace un año nos dijo que no quería hablar de Los Ángeles 2028 por respeto a sus compañeros. Viendo los resultados de este año, ¿ya se ve como deportista paralímpico en los próximos Juegos? R. Sí, me veo como deportista paralímpico. Hace un año no me gustaba hablar de ello por respeto a los deportistas españoles porque yo acababa de llegar y lo veía muy lejos. Pero es verdad que después de este y de mi posición en el ranking ya se puede verbalizar. Ya nos queda solamente un año, el 2027, para para puntuar y poder conseguir la plaza. Si me mantengo en el Top10 se podría decir que estamos dentro o si no, nos quedaría el Preolímpico. Ahora ya sí que la mirada está puesta en Los Ángeles. Ahora ya no hay miedo a hablarlo, estamos trabajando para ello. Ahora sí nos vemos ahí. P. ¿Qué siente cuándo piensa en LA2028? R. Siento un hormigueo cuando pienso en Los Ángeles de 2028. Cuando llego a al Centro de Alto Rendimiento de San Cugat (Barcelona) con la selección, hay un reloj con una cuenta atrás. Siempre lo miro con respeto. Hay un hormigueo, porque encima son Los Ángeles, que también es la cuna de la música rap. Yo empecé en el rap, entonces tiene ahí un doble componente que hace que se me pongan los pelos de escarpias. P. 2027 va a ser el año clave para lograr la clasificación. ¿Cuál es su hoja de ruta para conseguirlo? R. Es el último año para intentar puntuar y ganar nuestra plaza para los Juegos Paralímpicos. Y también es el Europeo en agosto. Si conseguimos ganar medalla serán muy buenos puntos para el ranking. Y luego pues iremos a los campeonatos internacionales que la Federación tenga preparados para nosotros, mínimo tenemos que ir a tres o cuatro para intentar sacar la mayor puntuación en individual y como equipo. P. ¿Va a ser su prioridad la boccia para conseguir la plaza para Los Ángeles? R. Sí, en el calendario hay los posibles campeonatos internacionales que ya saben en mis oficinas que en esas fechas no se pueden poner rodajes, ni una gira, ni una obra de teatro, etc. Y si consigo la plaza, en 2028 igual, para poder prepararme bien. P. Ayer la Reina Letizia recibió a la selección de boccia en el Palacio de la Zarzuela e incluso jugó a la boccia con usted. ¿Cómo fue la experiencia? R. La sensación que me llevo de nuestra visita a la Zarzuela es muy bonita. La reina Letizia ya conocía nuestro deporte desde los pasados Juegos Paralímpicos de París, donde mostró especial interés por la boccia, asistiendo a algunos partidos y compartiendo momentos con deportistas de nuestra selección. La audiencia fue tremendamente agradable. Me sorprendió gratamente el enorme interés que ha mostrado por nuestro deporte, por la selección española y, especialmente, por conocer de primera mano las dificultades y las barreras que nos encontramos en el camino. Quiso escuchar cuáles son nuestras necesidades, la falta de recursos, tanto para los técnicos y asistentes como para los propios deportistas, y todo aquello que necesitamos para seguir creciendo, dedicarle el máximo tiempo posible a nuestro deporte y poder competir al más alto nivel internacional. Se mostró muy cercana, con una empatía que sentí muy sincera. Nos felicitó por todos los logros conseguidos durante este año y, además, hemos tenido la oportunidad de hacer una demostración de boccia e incluso compartir una pequeña partida con ella en la propia Zarzuela. Más allá del reconocimiento deportivo, me quedo con su predisposición a escuchar, a conocer nuestra realidad y a entender las dificultades que afrontamos. Para mí, personalmente, fue una experiencia brutal. ¿Quién me iba a decir que algún día estaría en el Palacio de la Zarzuela, recibido por la Reina, y que sería precisamente por mi faceta como deportista representando a España? Es otra de esas bonitas sorpresas que me está regalando la vida a través de la boccia.

articles.title: Slaughtneil and Portaferry bid for Ulster honours
articles.summary: BBC Sport NI looks ahead to Saturday's Ulster Club SHC final between holders Slaughtneil and Down's Portaferry.
articles.body:
The biggest prize in Ulster club hurling is up for grabs in Armagh on Saturday [17:30 GMT] as Slaughtneil put their title on the line against Portaferry.

It will be their third meeting on the provincial stage in as many years, the first of those a thrilling 2024 final when Slaughtneil took home the Four Seasons Cup for the fifth time.

The Derry club won their second consecutive title last year with victory over St John's , defeating the Portaferry at the semi-final stage, but while they have dominated the fixture, it has not always been straightforward.

Paul McCormack's side moved straight from their 14th-straight Derry success into Saturday's final, while their opponents on Saturday from Down had a semi-final against Dunloy to navagate to reach the provincial showpiece.

Can Slaughtneil win a first provincial three in a row?

When the Robert Emmett's club won their first Ulster title in 2016, it would prove to be the opening act of a dynasty on the provincial stage.

They repeated the following year, won again in 2019 and 2021 with Covid-19 decimating the club season in the intervening year.

After defeats in the 2022 and 2023 finals, Michael McShane stepped away as manager with former Armagh dual star Paul McCormack taking up the reins and they have reasserted themselves as Ulster hurling's top dogs.

On Saturday, they have the opportunity to break new ground with a first three-peat at this level, but that "hasn't been mentioned" according to team captain Conor McAllister who is hopeful the "intensity in training" will have them ready for battle after waiting 10 weeks since capturing their county title.

While Slaughtneil are on the cusp of another piece of history with a seventh title which would put them above Ballycastle into fourth on the Ulster roll of honour, Portaferry are seeking just their second.

The St Patrick's club's one and only title came in 2014, and survivors from that day include team captain Matthew Conlan, Caolan Taggart and Eoghan Sands, while Connor O'Prey is now manager as they try to bridge a 12-year gap.

Conlan is now one of the experienced members of the team but that maiden success led him to believe "this happens all the time".

It hasn't been the case for Portaferry as Conlan accepts Slaughtneil "came and they have stayed".

Mageean's passing and past heartbreak fuels the Ports

Portaferry's semi-final victory over Dunloy came just two weeks after the passing of two-time Olympian Ciara Mageean, a native of the Ards peninsula town and former camogie player with the club.

"That win was for her," said corner forward Finn Turpin - who scored six points against the Antrim champions in the last four - as Portaferry capped an emotional day with a performance befitting of the occasion.

It was also the club's first championship win outside of their home county since the 2014 success, beaten at the first hurdle on three of the last four occasions by Slaughtneil and once by Cushendall in 2023, after extra time.

They saw an eight-point lead in the 2024 final evaporate, while last year at the semi-final stage , it was a little less dramatic as they fell to a five-point defeat, a game "we didn't perform anywhere near where we should be", according to team captain Conlan who feels they must "take it up a notch" this week.

Manager Connor O'Prey has endured the disappointments as a player and reflecting on "games we left behind" on the provincial stage, hopes lessons from those past disappointments "might benefit Portaferry to get over the line" this week.

Portaferry's intensity against Dunloy was a key ingredient to their victory but that ability to sustain it was not achieved overnight.

O'Prey, who suceeded Gerard McGrattan as manager this year, has applied some "subtle differences" to their approach but there has also been continuity with Luke Conlan, who plays for Cliftonville in the Irish League and a cousin of Matthew, has been retained as strength and conditioning coach.

While he insists Slaughtneil "probably don't get the credit for their standard of hurling", he is also aware that the Derry side are "physically really strong" and the "benchmark" of Ulster hurling.

To get over the line, they must match Slaughtneil in those aspects with Conlan's influence essential.

"Luke's Portaferry born and bred, a former club player and would probably have been an excellent senior hurler of the football didn't take off," O'Prey told BBC Sport NI.

"He's willing to go onto phone calls with the lads, has his own gym set up in the town, so he is bringing boys in during the off-season if they want to train collectively.

"His knowledge of the conditioning side of it is first class and he would say to me at the start of each week, 'this is what we need to be working on'."

Rogers cleared but Slaughtneil have injury doubts

The good news for Slaughtneil is the hugely influential Brendan Rogers is free to play after winning his appeal from a red card issues during the Derry final.

However, manager Paul McCormack is sweating on the fitness of Finn McEldowney who suffered a knee injury in the Derry SFC and Saturday "may come too early for him", while Ruairi O'Mianain remains sidelined with an ACL knee injury.

Still, Slaughtneil have plenty of quality in reserve and know-how at this stage which gives McCormack the confidence "to back our players".

While he feels "a break of the ball here or there" have aided his side's recent provincial success, he is also wary of another "huge battle" in store against a Portaferry side determined to turn the tables.

"They have got better from last year, have a huge number of men playing at Joe McDonagh level with Down and could say they are setting the standard for Ulster hurling, having beaten Antrim twice this year.

"Watching them at the Athletic Grounds two weeks ago [against Dunloy], that energy, drive and ability to punish teams - we've been trying to put a plan in place."
authors: David Mohan - BBC Sport NI journalist

articles.title: Tyson Fury’s wife backtracks on claim boxer suffers from schizophrenia
articles.summary: Paris Fury had claimed mental health diagnosis for Tyson following his 2015 victory over Ukraine’s Wladimir Klitschko.
articles.body:
Paris Fury, the wife of Tyson Fury, has retracted her claim that the British heavyweight was diagnosed with schizophrenia just months after he was crowned world champion in 2015.

In clips promoting a Netflix documentary, the boxer spoke about his mental health struggles following his victory over Ukraine’s Wladimir Klitschko in Germany.

Paris Fury said Tyson Fury had “mild schizophrenia” in an initial version of the documentary, which will be released on Friday.

Netflix said it had worked to “update” the footage in light of her clarification.

Fury, 38, is due to face Anthony Joshua in a long-awaited all-British showdown in Cardiff on December 11.

Paris Fury’s comments come after the British Boxing Board of Control indicated that it was investigating the earlier comments, though Robert Smith, the board’s general secretary, told the BBC it was “fairly confident” he would be cleared to fight Joshua.

“I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary,” Paris said in a statement.

“I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson’s condition and I used the word ‘schizophrenic’. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn’t have this condition and has never received a diagnosis.

“Mental health is complex, and it isn’t always easy to find the right words, especially when you’re living it with someone you love.

“I’m so proud of Tyson for really opening up in this documentary and want to say thank you for all the support we’ve received as a family.”

Fury has been open about his mental health struggles since beating Klitschko, after which he took a break of nearly three years from boxing.

His weight ballooned while he battled suicidal thoughts and drug and alcohol problems.

Fury admitted hearing “voices in my mind” following his win, adding: “Words can’t explain the darkness I was in.

“I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100 percent thought at times I’d end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much.”

Fury became world heavyweight champion for a second time when he beat WBC champion Deontay Wilder in February 2020.

Despite losing twice to Oleksandr Usyk in 2024, the only losses in his 39-fight professional career, Fury could become a three-time world champion when he takes on Joshua with the vacant WBA title set to be on the line.

Netflix said in a statement: “Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson’s official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch.”

articles.body:
There's nothing like an NHL fight. It brings the crowd to its feet, with two hockey players throwing haymakers to take an already intense game to another level.

The 2026-27 season has seen an increase in fights , with players willing to drop the gloves and go at it.

And this week seemed packed full of rough-and-tumble scraps. So with that in mind, we thought it'd be fun to look back and rank the best fights from the past week.

Disagree with our ranking? Submit your thoughts now in the comments section of the app.

This is a quick, intense scrap, but lacks the intensity of some of the others on the list.

This scrap features two old veterans going at it, with plenty of experience of dropping the gloves.

The second of the two Foligno brothers on our list, Nick Foligno squares off against Liam O'Brien and manages to knock his helmet off in this spirited fight.

This one features a David vs. Goliath matchup, with Adam Klapka serving as Goliath at 6-foot-8 and 238 pounds . Boucher holds is own against his bigger opponent, and even manages to knock Klapka's helmet off.

Some heavy punches were thrown here between Utah's McBain and Minnesota's McCarron, as the second fight from Wednesday's Wild-Mammoth game is featured on the list.

Another tough tussle featuring grizzled NHL vets, Ben Chiarot and Brayden Schenn swing for the fences in a matchup featuring two 35-year-olds.

You might not get anything better than this throughout the season.

This is an old-fashioned slugfest featuring two tough customers going for over a minute.

articles.title: Reigns Addresses 'Selfish' Criticism, Cody Rhodes' Wild WWE Travel Schedule, Rumors on Hardy Boys
articles.summary: Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.
articles.body:
Bleacher Report catches you up on the latest news from the WWE Universe.

Reigns Reveals His Pro Wrestling Philosophy

The Success Behind WWE's Team USA vs. Team Mexico 💪

Many top stars over the course of pro wrestling history have been accused of only being concerned with their own positioning and well-being, but Roman Reigns made it clear recently that he does not believe he belongs in that camp.

In a video posted Wednesday on Reigns' official YouTube account (h/t H Jenkins of Ringside News), Reigns pushed back against any narratives of him being a selfish performer:

"I'm not a selfish performer," Reigns said. "I'm not like someone who's just trying to get my ... Whatever is going to tell the best story out there, whatever is going to make them come unglued and come alive, no matter where I'm at on the card, if it's been a whole bunch of stuff out there that they've seen and we got to go out there and, you know, throw curveballs at them, then I'll do it.

"But that's what it's all about. I've been loading. I've been waiting to give y'all this. It's been in there, man. And sometimes you just got to, you know, you got to follow the assignment, do what needs to be done."

Reigns' comments came following his match against WWE champion Sami Zayn at the Crown Jewel premium live event in Saudi Arabia earlier this month.

In the main event of the show, Reigns beat Zayn in a tightly contested match to win the Crown Jewel Championship.

Reigns and Zayn entered the bout with no shortage of history, as Zayn was previously a member of The Bloodline and lent a helping hand to Reigns in many of his title defenses.

Despite the tension that has existed between them since Zayn turned on Reigns and left The Bloodline, they showed their respect for each other at Crown Jewel.

After Reigns' victory, he hugged Zayn and made it clear that he appreciated everything Zayn did for him in the past.

Although Reigns won the match, he showed it was possible to put over an opponent in a different way.

The OTC has done his fair share of winning and will continue to do so, but his comments suggest he is always thinking about delivering the best possible story and moments for the fans regardless of the match results.

Rhodes Potentially In Line for Tough Travel Schedule

If Cody Rhodes is part of the Wrestlepalooza premium live event in Perth, Australia, on Dec. 12, then he could be in for a difficult couple of days on the travel front.

Rhodes was selected by John Cena to partake in the John Cena Classic, which will be held at the ESPN Wide World of Sports Complex in Orlando, Florida, on Dec. 14.

At the same time, Rhodes is being advertised for WWE events in Australia in the days leading up to the John Cena Classic.

While no specific Superstars have been advertised for Wrestlepalooza yet, Rhodes is being advertised for the Dec. 9 live event in Melbourne and the Dec. 11 SmackDown in Perth.

According to Booking.com , the average flight time from Perth, Australia, to Orlando, Florida, is over 31 hours with stops factored in. Even a nonstop flight would still take about one entire day.

Despite being one of WWE's top stars, it is possible Rhodes could be held off Wrestlepalooza. However, even if Rhodes leaves Australia for the United States right after SmackDown, it wouldn't give him much time to recuperate from potential jet lag before competing in the John Cena Classic.

Rhodes prides himself on being WWE's "QB1," though, and figures to be up to the challenge regardless of any trials and tribulations he faces in terms of travel.

Latest on TNA, Outside Interest in Hardy Boyz

The Hardy Boyz are reportedly expected to have no shortage of suitors if and when their TNA contracts expire.

According to Fightful Select (h/t Steve Carrier of Ringside News), Matt and Jeff Hardy's TNA deal are set to expire soon, and re-signing them is viewed as a "priority" within TNA.

However, other wrestling companies are reportedly expected to "reach out to gauge possible work they could do with the Hardys as well."

Fightful added that despite the fact Matt is 52 years old and Jeff is 49, The Hardy Boyz "are not expected to slow down, and are looking to continue wrestling."

Regarded by many as the greatest tag team of all time, Matt and Jeff Hardy have held tag team titles together in several major companies, including WWE, TNA and Ring of Honor.

Matt and Jeff returned to TNA in 2024 after a stint in AEW, and they have continued their run of success, holding the TNA World Tag Team Championships three times since returning.

The Hardy Boyz also had a run in NXT thanks to the working relationship between TNA and WWE, briefly holding the NXT Tag Team Championships.

Both WWE and TNA figure to be viable options for The Hardy Boyz if they hit free agency, but a return to AEW or a move to another promotion could be on the table as well.

articles.title: Final Picks for Bloodline vs. 946, USA vs. Mexico and WWE Survivor Series WarGames 2026 Match Card
articles.summary: WWE Survivor Series is one of WWE's longest-running events, and in recent years, it has been home to the WarGames stipulation.
articles.body:
WWE Survivor Series is one of WWE's longest-running events, and in recent years, it has been home to the WarGames stipulation.

Some years, the traditional elimination match hasn't had a presence, but this year will see Cody Rhodes and Rey Mysterio lead teams into battle in a 5-on-5 match.

We will also see Liv Morgan defend the women's world title against Becky Lynch, and both the men's and women's WarGames matches.

The card only has four bouts scheduled, but with three of them including 10 Superstars apiece, they will likely be longer than usual.

Let's go through each match and make some predictions.

Liv Morgan is set to defend the Women's World Championship against Becky Lynch this weekend in the only singles bout on the entire card.

Their feud has been going on and off for years, which Lynch referenced in her most recent promo when bringing up that Morgan debuted on the main roster by attacking her with The Riott Squad.

Morgan has only held the belt since Money in the Bank on October 10, so it feels early, but Stephanie Vaquer's reign was even shorter, so we are going out on a limb with this one.

We're picking Lynch to win the belt for a very specific reason that will become clear in the next section.

Judgment Day once had a tight grip on Raw with multiple titles, but the group has been on a downward trajectory in recent months.

It feels like members of the group have different goals, and one person who has a good reason to separate from the group is Roxanne Perez.

The Prodigy has been playing backup to Morgan, and now Raquel Rodriguez, and it's time she steps out on her own. The timing feels right.

Turning on Morgan to cost her title would initiate a feud that needs to end with Perez defeating Morgan before moving on to pursue her own goals again.

Rey Mysterio, Dragon Lee, Penta, Rey Fenix and El Grande Americano all seem to be on the same page, but the same cannot be said for Team USA.

Cody Rhodes, CM Punk, Je'Von Evans and LA Knight seemed to have a good thing going, but then Seth Rollins was revealed as the final member on Monday.

Punk's reaction told the whole story. He and Rollins have a bitter rivalry, and being on the same team is going to make it difficult to work together.

The story here is simple: Punk and Rollins will have issues, and Team Mexico will capitalize on that to get the victory.

Most Likely WWE Survivor Series Face and Heel Turns

The Success Behind WWE's Team USA vs. Team Mexico 💪

Charlotte Flair and Jade Cargill will serve as the captains of the women's WarGames teams this weekend.

Flair will have Alexa Bliss, Tatum Paxley, Stephanie Vaquer and Bayley on her side, while Cargill has Jacy Jayne, Fallon Henley, Lainey Reid and Michin backing her up.

While the teams seem like an even match on a physical level, the level of combined experience on each side is very different.

Flair's team consists of four former world champions with more combined experience by a wide margin.

Even though it would benefit Cargill's team more, Flair's team is going to get the win simply because it makes the most sense.

The Bloodline will battle 946 in what is arguably the biggest match of the night, which means it will also have the greatest impact on future stories for a lot of the people involved.

Despite there being 10 men in the match, this is really about Roman Reigns and Royce Keys. The OTC sees Keys as a threat and wants to take him out before he establishes himself, but Keys is hoping to make his career by beating Reigns.

The Usos, Carmelo Hayes, Jacob Fatu, and maybe even Mike Santana will provide the high-flying excitement. Guys like OTM and Solo Sikoa will be the ones doing the catching.

Booking The Bloodline to win would immediately diminish 946's credibility, and WWE clearly wants the group to be a strong presence, so that is why we see Keys and his group getting the win.

It will likely be one of the Usos who takes the pin so Reigns stays protected heading into his eventual one-on-one clash with Keys.

Jaida Parker will not be inside the cage this weekend, but she will likely be at ringside to support her team, and possibly hand them weapons through the openings in the cage.

She could be a difference maker for her side in the fight, but this also feels like the perfect opportunity for The Bloodline to bring in someone to neutralize her.

Naomi's connection to The Bloodline has never been hidden by WWE. Her marriage to Jimmy Uso makes her a built-in ally who would be perfect to take on Parker.

This would lead to a singles match eventually, and it would be a great way to get Parker active on the main roster while also giving Naomi a storyline for her return.

articles.title: Updated 2026 WWE Survivor Series Card and Predictions for Match Order
articles.summary: WWE will continue its Thanksgiving Week tradition Saturday when the Survivor Series premium live event descends Saturday evening on Houston.
articles.body:
WWE will continue its Thanksgiving Week tradition Saturday when the Survivor Series premium live event descends Saturday evening on Houston.

The show will be headlined by a pair of WarGames matches with The Bloodline taking on 946 and a team led by Charlotte Flair facing a team led by Jade Cargill.

Additionally, the traditional, five-on-five elimination match is making its return in the form of Team USA vs. Team Canada, and Liv Morgan will defend the Women's World Championship against Becky Lynch in the only title bout of the night.

Final Picks for WWE Survivor Series WarGames 🔮

Most Likely WWE Survivor Series Face and Heel Turns

The Success Behind WWE's Team USA vs. Team Mexico 💪

Here is a complete rundown of the Survivor Series 2026 card, along with predictions for the match order.

Survivor Series 2026 Card and Projected Match Order

WarGames Match: Charlotte Flair, Alexa Bliss, Tatum Paxley, Bayley & Stephanie Vaquer vs. Jade Cargill, Michin, Jacy Jayne, Fallon Henley & Lainey Reid

Traditional 5-on-5 Elimination Match: Team USA (Cody Rhodes, CM Punk, Je'Von Evans, LA Knight & Seth Rollins) vs. Team Mexico (Rey Mysterio, Rey Fenix, Penta, Dragon Lee & El Grande Americano)

Women's World Championship: Liv Morgan (c) vs. Becky Lynch

WarGames Match: The Bloodline (Roman Reigns, Jey Uso, Jimmy Uso, Solo Sikoa & Jacob Fatu) vs. 946 (Royce Keys, Bronco Nima, Lucien Price, Carmelo Hayes & Cruz Montana)

The most heated feud in pro wrestling will finally come to a head Saturday at Survivor Series when The Bloodline and 946 clash in a WarGames match.

For the past few months, The Bloodline has been firmly in 946's crosshairs, and 946 has gotten the upper hand more often than not thanks to constant additions to the group, including Jaida Parker, Carmelo Hayes and Cruz Montana.

The Bloodline received a huge boost a couple of weeks ago, though, when Jacob Fatu returned to the fold after missing several weeks on the heels of Parker hitting him with a car.

As a unit, The Bloodline has a ton of experience in WarGames matches, which potentially gives it the edge heading into Survivor Series.

However, 946 will be hungry to make a statement, especially since a win could potentially position Royce Keys for an eventual World Heavyweight Championship match against Roman Reigns.

Given that it will be 946's first major match together as a group, it likely needs the win more than The Bloodline, but The Bloodline can never be counted out, especially when considering the faction's long history of success.

While not as deeply rooted in hatred as The Bloodline vs. 946, the women's WarGames match at Survivor Series has a chance to be a highly entertaining contest in its own right.

The rivalry between Charlotte Flair and Jade Cargill is the nucleus of the match, but there are plenty of other intriguing elements as well, including Alexa Bliss and Tatum Paxley's recent run-ins with both Fatal Influence and Cargill's group involving Michin and B-Fab.

On top of that, Flair added some major star power to her team in recent weeks with Bayley and Stephanie Vaquer entering the fray, which likely swung the pendulum in Charlotte's favor.

Cargill's team is young and hungry, though, and several of the members will be competing in the biggest match of their lives at Survivor Series.

Although it is difficult to envision such a star-studded team losing, Cargill's team has plenty to gain with a win, so that possibility cannot be completely ruled out.

Traditional 5-on-5 Elimination Match: Team USA vs. Team Mexico

For many years, the traditional, five-on-five elimination match was a Survivor Series staple, but it has gone dormant recently due to WarGames becoming a key part of the event.

However, this year, the five-on-five elimination match is back, and it will be contested alongside the two WarGames matches on the Survivor Series card.

In a unique twist, five of the best WWE Superstars Mexico has to offer will take on five of the United States' best with Rey Mysterio and Cody Rhodes serving as the captains.

A huge wrinkle was added Monday night on Raw when Rhodes revealed Seth Rollins as the last member of Team USA, much to the disapproval of CM Punk, who had been loving his role as co-captain of the team up until that moment.

Punk and Rollins have a checkered history, and their issues with each other figure to play a role in Saturday's bout, which adds another layer of intrigue to the proceedings.

articles.title: WWE's Team USA vs. Team Mexico Proves the Old Formula Still Works
articles.summary: WWE is reviving an annual tradition as Team USA prepares to take on Team Mexico in a five-on-five Survivor Series match.
articles.body:
WWE is reviving an annual tradition as Team USA prepares to take on Team Mexico in a five-on-five Survivor Series match.

For the past four years, the WarGames matches have been the centerpiece of the company's final "Big Four" premium live event of the year. The stipulation offered a welcome change of pace as the yearly battle for brand supremacy grew stale.

However, WWE has struggled to justify its use, and the final product has felt formulaic. Even more, the last few iterations haven't preserved the tone and intensity of the iconic steel cage match Dusty Rhodes introduced in 1987.

Final Picks for WWE Survivor Series WarGames 🔮

Most Likely WWE Survivor Series Face and Heel Turns

Team USA vs. Team Mexico has been a pleasant surprise, reminding fans the tried-and-true formula is still effective.

Lucha Libre's steady rise in popularity and the partnership with AAA made this the perfect time to showcase the company's best masked wrestlers. Meanwhile, Cody Rhodes and CM Punk's uneasy friendship has provided enough drama to keep the matchup interesting.

Team Mexico will undoubtedly be entertaining. Rey Mysterio, the greatest luchador of all time, will lead a five-man team of some of the most breathtaking performers on the roster.

Penta has been white hot this year. His World Heavyweight Championship match against Roman Reigns in Mexico City signaled his arrival as a bona fide main eventer, setting him up to win the men's Money in the Bank ladder match.

Rey Fenix is on a tremendous run as the AAA World Cruiserweight Champion. With 16 successful title defenses over 180 days, he finally found his groove with WWE. It will be a treat to see him team up with his brother, Mysterio, and Dragon Lee.

The reigning AAA Mega Champion, El Grande Americano, is a bit of an outlier because he's not actually Mexican. Still, the comedy gimmick has proven to be a massive hit for AAA and WWE in Mexico.

Team USA will have a tough night, trying to match their speed and work rate. It will be fun to watch them play off each other on Saturday night.

Rhodes and Punk bring the star power for Team USA, and their underlying tension has added an intriguing layer to their comedic segments.

Friction has been brewing between the two since Punk returned to win the Undisputed WWE Championship during the June 6 episode of Raw. It didn't come to a head at SummerSlam, but the inconclusive finish to their match ensured that their feud wasn't over.

Rhodes is determined to assert himself as team captain and reclaim his spot as QB1. Punk is seemingly oblivious to any lingering tension. He was legitimately enjoying putting together a squad with someone he still considers a friend until Seth Rollins entered the fray.

The Chicago native's reaction to the reveal that Rollins is the team's fifth member was priceless. For the first time since he returned to WWE, Punk didn't have to contend with his past. Now he has to work with his most bitter rival, who, as you would expect, reveled in the situation.

This has immediate implications for the lead-in to WrestleMania 43, and we can wait to see how they will coexist. We could be on the road to a rematch between Rhodes and Punk on The Grandest Stage of Them All.

This kind of storytelling and varied talent made Survivor Series stand out. It's nice to see a fresh take on its titular five-on-five match.

Hopefully, this proves WWE can continue to reimagine this concept for years to come.

articles.title: England’s Overton takes 5-12 as Australia bowled out for record low in T20
articles.summary: Australia are bowled out for 108 as Jamie Overton claims career-best figures in England’s seven-wicket win in Brisbane.
articles.body:
Jamie Overton took a career-best 5-12 as England thrashed Australia by seven wickets in the third T20 international in Brisbane on Friday.

Overton’s figures were the best by an Englishman against Australia in T20s as the home side were bundled out for 108, their lowest score on Australian soil.

“I thought Jamie Overton was outstanding tonight,” England captain Harry Brook said.

“He’s worked hard and put in some extra graft at training.

“He simplified his game and reaped the rewards tonight – he had it on a string and it felt like we could change the field and make them make a mistake.”

Brook won the toss and sent Australia in to bat, and off-spinner Liam Dawson struck early when he had Australian skipper Mitch Marsh caught at mid-on.

Jake Fraser-McGurk and Sam Harper attacked during the powerplay, taking the score to 55 after five overs.

Harper raced to 26 off 14 balls before Dawson grabbed his second when the Australian wicketkeeper got a top edge to Overton at mid-on.

Overton then swung into action with the ball, claiming the next five wickets as Australia slumped from 65-2 to 92-7 and then collapsed to 108 all out when Sam Curran clean-bowled Billy Stanlake.

Aneurin Donald, who smashed 85 off 32 on the Gold Coast on Tuesday, got the run chase off to a spectacular start, belting 31 from just 11 balls.

But a rain delay seemed to help the Australians, as Brook holed out for nine after play resumed, before Donald fell for 32, leaving England 49-3.

Another rain break threatened to stop England’s momentum again, but Jordan Cox blasted 33 in quick time to give the visitors an easy win and go ahead in the five-game series 2-1.

Marsh conceded that Australia were outplayed by a better team.

“No excuses, we’ve got to be better,” he said.

“We’ve all played Big Bash games here (at the Gabba).

“You have to give yourself the chance to cash in at the back end (of the innings), but we didn’t get near that tonight.”

The two teams head to Sydney for the fourth game on Sunday night.

articles.title: Jaguars Determine WR Parker Washington's Week 12 Status

articles.body: Jacksonville Jaguars wide receiver Parker Washington won't play Sunday against the Tennessee Titans (1 p.m. ET on FOX) after injuring a shoulder in practice. Coach Liam Coen ruled out Washington on Friday, a day after being hurt in practice, and said he is considered "week to week." Washington leads the Jaguars (7-3) with 44 receptions for 748 yards and six touchdowns. He caught 58 passes for 847 yards and five scores in 2025, becoming quarterback Trevor Lawrence’s go-to guy down the stretch. A sixth-round draft pick out of Penn State in 2023, Washington is in the final year of his rookie contract and could be a candidate for the team’s franchise tag if the sides can’t agree to a long-term deal before March 3, 2027. His absence could mean more snaps for rookie Josh Cameron, Brian Thomas Jr. and potentially two-way standout Travis Hunter. Jakobi Meyers is likely to become Jacksonville's No. 1 receiver against the Titans (1-9) and maybe longer. Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Why snooker could be the most mentally challenging sport
articles.summary: With Mark Allen the latest snooker player to talk about his mental health struggles, BBC Sport looks at why the sport is so mentally challenging - and what is being done to help.
articles.body:
It is perhaps one of the most visceral and deeply human interviews that any sportsperson has ever given.

When Mark Allen, snooker's world number 11, spoke live on TNT Sports , external in October, he said he was in a "bad place", that he didn't see a future in the game, and that he was "just trying to survive".

Allen had just been beaten at the Northern Ireland Open. It was his first match since the World Championship, when in May he was one black ball away from a place in the final.

He has not spoken publicly since. In a post on social media in early November, Allen said the future is "looking brighter", , external although this week he explained he was having a "very tough" time , external and was "definitely stuck in a major low right now".

While Allen has not publicly discussed the reasons for his struggles, and if it is related to the sport, he had previously said "there is more to life than just a career".

And this would be far from the first time that poor mental health has affected a snooker player.

Right from the 1970s and the sport's first television boom, some of its great characters have spoken openly, and regularly, about addiction, isolation and snooker's unique psychological challenges.

So what is it about the sport that makes it so mentally difficult? And what is being done to help?

If you are affected by any of the issues raised in this story you can visit BBC Action Line, which has details of a range of advice and support.

Why is snooker so 'mentally destructive'?

In his emotional interview, Allen said he had spent 10 weeks in a mental health clinic and discharged himself to play in Belfast, though he planned to continue his treatment.

Other players have also previously spoken candidly about their own struggles, including multiple world champions Ronnie O'Sullivan and Mark Selby.

Selby considered retirement after a first-round defeat at the 2024 World Championship, while in 2025 O'Sullivan said many players "suffer in silence".

Snooker is, perhaps alongside golf, one of the most intensely individual sports, where players spend long hours alone in dimly lit practice rooms or travelling on the road, and where entire livelihoods can come down to tiny misjudgements.

"At least in golf you have your own ball. You don't have to worry about anyone else," 1997 world champion Ken Doherty told BBC Sport.

"In snooker, when you're sitting in your chair and your opponent is at the table, you can do nothing. Only sit and bear it.

"That is the toughest part about our sport and mentally that is quite difficult for people to comprehend."

Dr Paul Gaffney is a psychologist who has worked with Allen for the past four seasons. Snooker players, he says, can feel like they are inside a "colosseum".

"There are people looking down at you, and you can absolutely thrive, or be beaten in front of the world stage."

Allen considers retirement after NI Open exit

Selby faces tough UK opener, with Allen set to feature

Gary Wilson, the world number 28, has also spoken openly about the bouts of depression he has suffered during his 22-year career.

"It's a very lonely sport," the 41-year-old told BBC Sport.

"You're practising in a club and you could be in there on your own for six, seven, eight hours a day in a dark room, with just a snooker light on.

"It can get unhealthy mentally in itself, but it's what you've got to do. You've got to dedicate yourself to it.

"I think it is a more mentally destructive sport, potentially, than a lot of other individual sports."

When asked how he felt watching Allen's interview, Wilson said: "We can all relate.

"There are a lot of lads who are a lot lower down on the tour struggling.

"Every couple of years, this coming out and nothing being done about it, isn't really good enough."

What is being done to help - and is it enough?

Since 2021, snooker's governing body, the World Professional Billiards and Snooker Association (WPBSA), has put mental health provisions in place for players in the form of a partnership with Sporting Chance, a charity founded by former Arsenal and England footballer Tony Adams.

In the five years since the partnership was formed, Sporting Chance has provided more than 180 sessions of counselling for a wide range of issues.

Players experiencing mental health issues are encouraged to ring a confidential 24/7 helpline, and Sporting Chance will then arrange free treatment with a qualified therapist. This can take place over six to 12 talking sessions.

But some players believe that support could go further. In an interview in January 2025, O'Sullivan and Selby said they would like to see mental health professionals operate on-site at tournaments.

"I think players would have a lot more inclination to use somebody physically there at tournaments. I don't know how feasible that is," said Wilson.

There are benefits and drawbacks to the Sporting Chance service. Players receive a bespoke counsellor, rather than one who may speak to every player, but they are required to reach out themselves for this through a helpline. Doherty, who sits on the WPBSA players' board, believes it is the best solution.

"Players don't necessarily want to go and speak to someone at a tournament," Doherty said.

"We thought about having someone on hand, but then we thought, we don't think anyone would use it.

"This is a free service. Nobody has to know. Nobody will know on the circuit. It's just you and the person you're talking to.

"I know Ronnie [O'Sullivan] and Mark [Selby] spoke about that, but they obviously didn't know that service was there for them, that it's free, and that it's available for the whole tour."

WPBSA chairman Jason Ferguson, a former professional player himself, said: "The highs are very high and the lows are very low.

"If there's anything we can work on, it's continually getting the message out to other players to say those services are there."

In 2021, Wilson said he felt "totally gone" when the depression he explained he was suffering with came to a head in a match against John Higgins.

Wilson missed a pot, and while still down on his shot, thrashed the cue ball into a neighbouring red, , external sending the frame into chaos. He was fined £250 and received a formal warning.

But Wilson - known as the Tyneside Terror - believes there could be a more liberal approach to such displays of emotion in this most gentlemanly of sports.

"You're expected to keep your emotions completely in check at all times," he said.

"Now that's just not sport. When you look at any other sport that you play… you've got to be able to vent."

In response, Ferguson said that while snooker's authorities and fans love to see such passion, fundamentally it is a sport of "great etiquette".

Allen is next due to play in the UK Championship - a tournament he won in 2022 - which starts on Saturday. He has been drawn against qualifier Yuan Sijun but has not spoken publicly about whether he will play.

For Dr Gaffney, watching Allen's interview at Belfast's Waterfront venue was "painful". It made him feel "sadness, but also admiration".

"The brilliant thing about what he's done - his courage, his integrity, his class in the last few weeks - is there will be people watching snooker who wouldn't have been watching snooker before, because Mark Allen is playing," said Dr Gaffney, "and I think that says everything about the man."

articles.title: Michigan Reportedly Starting QB Bryce Underwood Against Ohio State
articles.summary: Michigan has reportedly made a decision on which of Bryce Underwood or Tommy Carr will start The Game against Ohio State.
articles.body: Bryce Underwood lost the starting job as Michigan's quarterback when Tommy Carr won it for the Wolverines against Penn State in Week 6, but he'll get a chance to redeem his season against archrival Ohio State, per ESPN. Underwood is reportedly the starter in rivalry week's Michigan-Ohio State catchup, giving him a chance to bring Michigan to 7-5 in Big Ten play — the same record that the Buckeyes would have should they lose on Saturday. Carr was a disappointment for Michigan as a starter in all but one game, in which he thrived against Rutgers. (Albeit a Rutgers team that opened its season with a loss to UMass.) He threw for just 167 yards against Indiana's tough defense, even with overtime, and failed to crack 200 combined yards in losses to Michigan State and Oregon — in the latter, Underwood also played and similarly struggled. Against UCLA, though, Underwood got the start, and despite throwing for just 127 yards and completing 45.8% of his passes, it was enough to convince head coach Kyle Whittingham that the sophomore deserves to close out Michigan's season against its top rival. In nine games, Underwood has 85 completions in 156 attempts for 1,077 passing yards. He has six touchdowns and six interceptions, with all of his numbers tumbling from his freshman campaign with the Wolverines. articles.title: Demario Davis Explains Why Aaron Glenn Is Right Coach For Jets
articles.summary: New York Jets linebacker Demario Davis gave a strong public backing for head coach Aaron Glenn.
articles.body: Demario Davis has played for seven head coaches across 15 seasons in the NFL with three teams, including three different stints with the New York Jets. He’s convinced Aaron Glenn is the right man to lead the Jets to success. Glenn, who was defensive coordinator with the Detroit Lions before taking the job, is just 6-22 since arriving in New York last year. But Davis, a two-time Pro Bowl linebacker, gave him a glowing endorsement. "I believe in AG’s vision because he’s been a part of an organization that was at the bottom and helped it ascend to greatness," Davis said on the AP’s "Football Unfiltered" podcast. "When you see the Detroit Lions now, I’ve been part of organizations that were down and part of the organization that were really high. I’ve been a leader in those organizations to be able to see it. And so when I came in, it was very easy to be captivated by the vision that the organization has for where it wants to go. And Aaron Glenn is the one who is leading that vision." The Jets went 3-14 in 2025 and have already matched that win total this season at 3-8. Davis began his career with the Jets in 2012 and played for Rex Ryan. He spent a season in Cleveland with the Browns playing for Hue Jackson before getting traded back to the Jets, where he played for Todd Bowles. He left for the New Orleans Saints and played for Sean Payton, Dennis Allen and Kellen Moore, going to the playoffs three times in eight seasons. He returned to New York in March. He had high praise not only for Glenn but owner Woody Johnson, general manager Darren Mougey and the rest of the front office. "Being in this market, one of the toughest markets, a super results-oriented, performance-based business, a lot of times people just look at the bottom line," Davis said. "But when you’re trying to build something successful, when you’re trying to build something sustainable, you have to build it with the right stuff. There has to be a level of grittiness to it, there has to be a level of resilience to it. There has to be a culture being put in place. "And that’s the thing that exists inside of the Jets’ building right now. There is a culture that’s there in a relatively short time. There’s a strong culture. There’s unity. There’s oneness and synchronization from the top to the bottom with the team owner, with the front office, with the coaching staff, with the players. … And, you know, AG is at the top of that." Reporting by The Associated Press.

articles.title: Matvei Michkov Suspended by Flyers For Canucks Game, Latest NHL Rumors Amid Trade Buzz
articles.summary: Star winger Matvei Michkov will be held out of the Philadelphia Flyers' home game against the Vancouver Canucks on Friday.
articles.body:
Star winger Matvei Michkov will be held out of the Philadelphia Flyers' home game against the Vancouver Canucks on Friday.

According to Elliotte Friedman of Sportsnet, "there is word" that Michkov is being suspended for Friday's contest due to a violation of team rules.

That comes in the wake of ESPN NHL insider Kevin Weekes' recent report that Michkov "would likely want a new start elsewhere" in the form of a trade out of Philadelphia.

Despite Michkov's reported desire to get traded, the Flyers have been resistant to that idea.

Friedman (h/t NHL Rumour Report ) reported two weeks ago that the Flyers view Michkov as a "long-term investment," and don't want to give up on him too soon.

Cutter Gauthier was used as an example since he forced his way out of Philly and is currently the NHL's leading goal scorer with the Anaheim Ducks.

After surprisingly making the playoffs last season, the Flyers have largely struggled so far this season with a 9-12-6 record. Their 24 points entering Friday's games place them 11th in the Eastern Conference.

The 21-year-old Michkov, who was the No. 7 overall pick in the 2023 NHL draft, has been one of the Flyers' biggest bright spots in a difficult season.

He leads the Flyers in both goals (11) and points (20) through 27 games played.

Without Michkov in the lineup on Friday, head coach Rick Tocchet will likely have to lean on the likes of Trevor Zegras, Travis Konecny, Porter Martone and Christian Dvorak for the bulk of Philly's offensive production.

articles.title: Bengals linebacker to wear special cleats honoring Fiona the hippo
articles.summary: Bengals linebacker Barrett Carter will wear special purple cleats honoring Fiona the hippo during Sunday's game against the Saints.
articles.body:
Bengals linebacker Barrett Carter will wear "Hippo Love" cleats to honor the Cincinnati Zoo & Botanical Garden 's most beloved Nile hippopotamus.

"This is near and dear to my heart," Carter said while holding purple cleats decorated with an illustration of Fiona, who . died Nov. 19 after swallowing a hat that fell into her enclosure days before.

"Spent a lot of quality time with Fiona," he said in the video shared by the Bengals. "Hearing about the news that she passed was really heartbreaking for me."

A child visiting the habitat was throwing the hat in the air and a ceiling fan caught it and propelled it into the habitat. An animal autopsy revealed the attempts to save her were ultimately futile .

The Bengals are scheduled to play the New Orleans Saints at 1 p.m. on Sunday, Nov. 29 at Paycor Stadium.

Fiona is also expected to receive a primetime TV shoutout one day earlier during the 100th Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade , which dedicated a blue balloon in her memory.
